# PROGRESS.md — Soloist State Ledger

> **This file is the shared memory across sessions.** Git history complements it, but this ledger is
> where a session reads what's done and what's next. **Read it at the start of every session** (per
> `CLAUDE.md` §1) and **update it at the end of every session** (per `CLAUDE.md` §10–§11). Keep it
> factual and evidence-backed — never mark `Verified` what you didn't verify.

> **LATEST (2026-08-31): LOCAL-CLI INTER-AGENT COLLABORATION RESEARCH — comprehensive
> replacement-oriented report complete; docs-only, no phase status changed.** The report is
> [`docs/research/local-cli-inter-agent-collaboration.md`](docs/research/local-cli-inter-agent-collaboration.md)
> (6,688 words, 64 unique primary-source links). It covers Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Kimi, Amp,
> OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Generic tools against Soloist's exact constraints: users'
> installed CLIs and existing setup/subscriptions, heterogeneous local teams, standardized
> send/receive/acknowledge, and no provider credential brokerage.
>
> **Decision established by the evidence:** do not repair the current idle-gated PTY wake path.
> `AgentMailbox::wake` ultimately reaches `PtyIo::write_all`; that is terminal input, not a provider
> session protocol, and the current real-window tests use synthetic IPC-polling agents rather than
> live Claude/Codex/Gemini/Kimi processes. Retain the bounded mailbox, authenticated scope, lineage,
> list/get/ack, completion correlation, transcript, and timer scheduling; replace autonomous
> message/timer/onboarding delivery with a durable collaboration broker plus capability-probed
> provider Turn Adapters. ACP is a reusable southbound adapter where implemented, MCP remains the
> agent-facing pull/ack plane, and A2A is a possible future external boundary but the wrong internal
> layer for installed local CLIs. **No PTY fallback.**
>
> **Provider gates:** prototype Kimi ACP, Copilot SDK, and Codex app-server/exec first. Codex
> app-server is rich but experimental; Kimi Web is optional/experimental behind ACP; Gemini/OpenCode/
> Amp require installed-version conformance probes; Generic requires an explicit semantic transport
> profile. Claude managed-team mode is **blocked** pending explicit Anthropic approval because the
> technically suitable Agent SDK path conflicts with the subscription-reuse constraint under
> Anthropic's published product policy; Channels fit the authenticated CLI better but remain a
> no-receipt research preview. Google policy for this exact cached-subscription orchestration also
> needs a recorded answer before Gemini GA. The active implementation work remains the bounded-file-
> watching branch below; this research changed no source or phase status.

> **LATEST (2026-08-28): BOUNDED PROJECT FILE WATCHING — twenty-two commits through `17f7fc5` on
> `fix/bounded-project-file-watching`, PR #198, `Done — pending verify`. Measured on real hardware:
> **57,596 watches / 8 inotify instances → 255 / 1** (~226x), dev build of this branch running
> alongside the installed one, same repo open in both.** Stacked on `feat/shadcn-adoption-and-working-shimmer` (PR #197),
> which is green in CI on all four e2e shards plus `check`/`bundle`/`smoke`.
>
> **Why.** Soloist exhausted the system inotify budget. Measured live: the installed build held
> **57,861 of 65,536** watches (88.3%) for a single project, and with tsserver the machine sat at
> 99.2% — currently failing every `crates/sys` test that registers a real watch. Not a leak (counts
> flat over 90s; every handle map has matching removes) but one unfiltered `RecursiveMode::Recursive`
> watch per project root, and inotify charges one watch per DIRECTORY. This repo is 58,179
> directories; excluding what git ignores, 337. A second open project (Laravel) holds 706,030
> gitignored dirs under `storage/`.
>
> **A cheaper primitive does not exist.** Git's `fsmonitor--daemon` runs on inotify on Linux and
> exposes no subscribable change stream; `fanotify`'s `FAN_MARK_FILESYSTEM` needs `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`,
> and unprivileged fanotify (5.13+) is per-inode. Raising `max_user_watches` is actively worse: it
> converts a bounded visible error into a permanent invisible drain, forcing `git status` over a
> 734k-directory repo against a 1s debounce ceiling. Design and sources recorded in
> `.scratch/bounded-file-watching/`.
>
> **Landed.** Per-path watch accounting so a refusal can clear (`68b7138`) — three parallel maps
> collapsed into one record, which is what let the bug exist; a session-based `FileWatcher` port so
> one inotify instance backs many paths (`8c8a423`), lifting the ~32-project `max_user_instances`
> ceiling; a gitignore-aware scanner over the `ignore` crate (`2daf8b1`, +896 bytes release,
> unwired — re-measure after T6); `ProjectWatchSet` planning a project's watches as a bounded set
> with a budget and incremental maintenance (`12d3783`); a `Degraded` limit state in the UI
> (`2c37c33`); fake levers for the unopenable-session path (`827f412`).
>
> **Review pass — eight further commits.** A two-axis code review (Standards + Spec) ran against the
> branch and every finding was implemented. **The watch budget had neither enforcement nor reclaim**
> (`dd82208`): `register` spent without ever checking the share, nothing released what a shrunk plan
> no longer wanted, and `absorb_appeared`'s `.max(1)` granted past the share — plus a degradation
> that never cleared on a *widening* share (the replan trigger was monotone toward degradation), and
> a scan ceiling counting **files** where the share counts **directories**. **A prefix-less restart
> glob** (`**/*.json`) had stopped watching the gitignored directories the old recursive root watch
> covered (`b15e466`); prefix scans are now fitted one at a time, named prefixes before the
> whole-root fallback. **Two error-semantics fixes:** `BudgetExhausted` claimed the *system's* limit
> was exhausted when Soloist's own share had refused (`e94f19a`), and a new `WatchError::ShareExhausted`
> (`17f7fc5`) lets the notice give the advice that actually applies — raising
> `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` lifts one and not the other; the degraded notice mis-attributed its
> cause the same way. **Structure:** the `WatchScanner` port moved from `filewatch`, which drives
> none of it, to `watchset`, and `git/watched.rs` → `routing.rs` (`5f6375d`); `Watches` → `Routes`,
> the type having held no watches since the watch-set collapse (`8b0cfcb`). The sampler flake
> recorded below is **fixed** (`0874ef0`). The new refusal reason's wire form is pinned beside every
> other one in `events_tests.rs`.
>
> **Measured (T7).** Watches via `grep -h '^inotify wd:' /proc/$pid/fdinfo/*`, instances via
> `find /proc/$pid/fd -lname 'anon_inode:inotify'`; pids cross-checked against the HTTP runtime file
> (installed :24678, dev :24679). Installed build **57,596 watches / 8 instances**; this branch
> **255 / 1**, re-confirmed 3x. Directory ground truth: 59,080 total, **315 gitignore-eligible** (via a
> standalone program replicating `watchscan.rs`'s exact `WalkBuilder` config, reproduced twice),
> `.claude/worktrees` 40,483 excluded via `.git/info/exclude`. Release binary at `304583f`
> **24,115,792 bytes**; `ignore` contributes **48.5 KiB** wired (`cargo bloat --crates`) — the earlier
> "+896 bytes" was measured unwired, when the linker dropped it.
>
> **One figure is unexplained and is not claimed otherwise.** The plan predicts ~343 watches
> (root + `.git` + 314 tree + ~27 refs); 255 were measured, 88 short. Ruled out: raw OS refusal by
> arithmetic (420 free before, 164 after), and "created after the scan" (several absent dirs are weeks
> old). Not identified — the repo was under concurrent edit, so inode cross-referencing is not
> trustworthy evidence. **Unknown.**
>
> **Not measured — five T7 steps are UNPERFORMED, not deferred with a plan.** Namely:
> **three-project simultaneity**; the **close/reopen leak cycle on a real machine** (covered only at
> the fake level, in `crates/core`); the **by-hand `mkdir` race**; **`just soak`**; and the
> **degraded/refused notice text**. The first four need a host whose inotify budget is not already
> consumed by the installed build — **this machine's is**, which is the condition the branch exists
> to remove. The notice text is blocked separately: Wayland blocks `wmctrl`/`xdotool` window
> addressing so the window cannot be driven, a full-desktop screenshot was declined for privacy, and
> the HTTP API exposes no watch-limit state (it is UI-only over the Tauri event bus). Also
> unmeasured: `just bundle-size`; a clean `main` binary diff. The "after" watch
> figure is a **debug** build. Stock `just dev-alongside` could not start — Vite's `beforeDevCommand`
> dies with `ENOSPC` because the installed build holds the budget; run with `CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=true`
> and `--no-watch`, which move unrelated tooling watchers off inotify without touching the subsystem
> under test.
>
> **RESOLVED — the `check` failure was the test's own setup, not production.**
> `config_watch.rs` wrote its edit before either spawned loop had been polled: `#[tokio::test]` is a
> current-thread runtime, `tokio::spawn` only schedules, and there was no `.await` between the spawns
> and the write — so both loops were provably unpolled, which is why it elapsed cleanly every time
> rather than flaking. `80e8d0e` had dropped the old test's explicit `yield_now()` synchronisation
> without replacing it for a path that now crosses a `supervise` spawn and an off-runtime scan.
> Isolated by inserting one 300ms sleep (3/3 green), then fixed by re-issuing the edit until the
> reload arrives or the existing budget elapses — free, since `ConfigEngine` hash-diffs. Retry period
> must exceed the reactor's 300ms quiet window or each retry re-arms the debounce (10/10 failures
> before that was understood). **`cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast` → 2058 passed
> across 55 binaries, 0 failures.**
>
> **Open follow-up — the startup window widened.** `ProjectWatchSet` registers through a multi-hop
> async chain (supervise-spawn → off-runtime scan → blocking `watch_dir`), up to ~300ms, where each
> reactor previously established its watch synchronously after one yield. Edge-triggered with no
> content rescan, so a `solo.yml` edit inside that window is lost permanently. Not believed
> user-visible (a human is slower than 300ms) but reachable by a script or a `git checkout` swapping
> `solo.yml` as a project opens; the retry-based test can no longer detect it widening. Candidate
> fixes: a readiness signal `load_project` callers await, or a re-read on first successful
> registration.
>

> **Verification lesson, recorded because it caused the above.** The gate is
> `cargo test --workspace --locked` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:50`). Narrow runs like
> `cargo test -p soloist-core --lib` structurally exclude every `tests/` integration target and cannot
> evidence a green branch. Locally, `--no-fail-fast` is also required: `cargo test --workspace` stops
> at the first failing binary, and `crates/pty`'s interactive-shell test flakes here, masking
> everything after it. Run correctly, the whole workspace has exactly one failure — the one above.
>
> **New finding — a partial watch failure is invisible.** `watchset/reconcile.rs:104-129` escalates
> only the project **root's** refusal to a reported `WatchLimit::Refused`; every other per-path failure
> emits `tracing::warn!` and continues. **No `tracing_subscriber` is initialized anywhere in
> `crates/app/src`** (grepped, confirmed absent), so those warnings produce zero output. Not reported,
> not logged, not countable — in a subsystem whose signature failure mode is silence. **Open follow-up.**
> Also open: `Registered.paths` is a `HashSet<PathBuf>`, erasing the priority order `plan()` builds.
>

> **LATEST (2026-08-27): DSA AUDIT SLICE 8 — E2E TEST ISOLATION — the developer's git configuration
> no longer reaches the app under test; mutation-proven, `just lint` exit 0, `just test` green.** On
> `main`, commits `a745889` (the fix) and `dabdc42` (an incidental lead-agent lockfile refresh the
> e2e build produced). Work item **S30-F1** at the verifier-narrowed scope, corroborated by S37-F1.
> **No product code changed** — `git diff --stat crates/` empty — because the product must honour a
> real user's configuration; the fix belongs in the harness.
>
> **The escape.** The app reads a repository by running the user's own `git`, and those invocations
> inherit the environment the service spawned the app with. The three existing isolation legs
> (`SOLOIST_APP_DATA_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`, the `dev.soloist.app.e2e` identifier) cover app state,
> webview storage and the single-instance lock, and **none of them touched git**. Every walk that put
> the app on a real repository therefore read the developer's real `~/.gitconfig` and
> `/etc/gitconfig`. `e2e/src/harness/repository.ts` had the same shape the Rust-side hole had: it
> neutralised the machine's configuration for the *harness's* own `execFileSync` and for nothing the
> app ran.
>
> **The unadjudicated question, answered empirically against the code (STEP 0).** S30-F1 is right and
> S37-F1 is wrong: credential prompting is **not** closed in product code on the path the window
> takes. `crates/git/src/runner.rs:117-121` sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` on every invocation, which
> closes terminal prompting only; `crates/git/src/sync.rs:106-109` applies the `UNATTENDED` set
> (`GIT_ASKPASS=""`, `SSH_ASKPASS=""`, `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, `GCM_INTERACTIVE=0`) **only** for
> `Prompting::Denied`, and `Prompting::Allowed` passes `&[]` — deliberately, because a person sitting
> in front of the window that asked should be asked. Verifier G's read is confirmed on both counts,
> including the second half: no e2e spec reaches a remote today (nothing under `e2e/specs/` or
> `e2e/src/` drives push/pull/fetch/publish; the exchange controls live in the window chrome and no
> screen drives them). So the rung is guard-less but unreached, and the harness is the only place it
> can be closed. It is closed now, before a walk reaches a remote rather than after one has.
>
> **The fix, three legs.** (1) `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` points at a configuration the run owns
> (`e2e/.tmp/git/config`, written by `onPrepare` after its wipe) and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` at
> `/dev/null`, both set at **module load** beside `PATH`/`SHELL` — the app inherits the launcher's
> environment, so a lifecycle hook is too late. (2) `GIT_ASKPASS`/`SSH_ASKPASS` emptied and
> `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`: these are read from the environment rather than from configuration, so
> leg 1 does not close them and a desktop session exporting one still hands `git` a window to open.
> (3) Every fixture repository resets `credential.helper` to empty and then names a recording stub of
> its own inside `.git/`, mirroring `crates/git/tests/fixture/mod.rs` — repo-local configuration binds
> the **adapter** too, because the adapter runs inside that repository. `repository.ts`'s now-redundant
> `CONFIG` constant is gone; `IDENTITY` stays and is load-bearing rather than defensive.
>
> **Test-first, and shown to fail.** The run's configuration is deliberately **not empty** — an app
> that never received it and one that received an empty one behave identically, so there would be
> nothing to assert. It names one `core.excludesFile` holding one path, and
> `e2e/specs/version-control/global-git-config.spec.ts` ("reports the path that configuration excludes
> as ignored, and its twin as an ordinary file") drives the app's own Files tab over a fixture holding
> two untracked files alike in every way the app can see. New screen reader `gitRail.projectFiles()`
> snapshots the rows in one evaluation. **Mutation pass:** with the two `process.env` lines removed
> the spec failed with `Expected value: {"ignored": true, "name": "draft-note.md"}` against
> `Received array: [… {"ignored": false, "name": "draft-note.md"} …]` — the app reporting a listing it
> could only produce by never having read the run's configuration. Restored byte-clean, re-run green.
>
> **Gates.** `pnpm -C e2e typecheck` clean. Targeted e2e run (no xvfb on this host — run on the live
> display; none of these specs assert focus): **4 spec files, 9 tests, all passing in 49 s** —
> `smoke`, the new `global-git-config`, `open-diff`, `tree-actions` (the two walks that put the app's
> git adapter on a real repository). `just lint` **exit 0**. `just test` **exit 0**: `cargo test
> --workspace` **2017 passed / 0 failed** across 54 result lines, `vitest` **172 files / 1283 tests
> passed**.
>
> **Full suite, run afterwards and green: `just e2e` — 18 spec files, 18 passed, 100% completed in
> 05:07, exit 0**, every walk under the run's own git configuration. `xvfb-run` was the smaller of two
> blockers: the recipe also refuses Node >= 26 (this host defaults to 26.3.0) because WebdriverIO
> 9.29.1 sets headers Node 26's undici rejects, so no WebDriver session can start. Run it through the

> targeted run had not covered all pass unchanged, so nothing on this machine was passing because of a
> personal git setting.
>
> **Deliberately out of scope, per the verifier:** the proposed `harness/sandbox.ts` `Sandbox` record
> / `sandboxEnv()`, overriding `HOME`, the `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`CACHE`/`STATE` set, collapsing the three

> **LATEST (2026-08-23): DSA AUDIT SLICE 3 — AUTOSAVE ACKNOWLEDGE-BEFORE-CLEAN + SINGLE-FLIGHT, AND
> THE SETTLE-GATED SETTINGS WRITE QUEUE — gate-green, `Done — pending verify`, UNCOMMITTED.** Work
> items **S27-F1** (`useAutosave`) and **S25-F1 commit 2** (`ProjectSettingsPane`'s write queue), from
> the DSA codebase audit held in the Soloist MCP scratchpads. `useAutosave` previously destroyed the
> pending value and set `dirty=false` **before** the write settled, so all four editors (scratchpad,
> todo, diagram, template) rendered "Saved" and disabled Save for text that was never written, and a
> Reload then discarded it. The verifier had established the fix had to span the store layer, because
> every store `save` already swallows its own rejection and always resolves.
>
> **Fix.** New `crates/app/ui/src/store/saveOutcome.ts` — closed union `type SaveOutcome = "saved" |
> "refused"`, the only signal a caller gets back since `save` never rejects. All four store hooks
> (`useScratchpadEditor`, `useTodoEditor`, `useDiagramEditor`, `useTemplateEditor`) now return
> `Promise<SaveOutcome>`. `useAutosave` (`crates/app/ui/src/components/editor/useAutosave.ts`) is
> rebuilt around one discriminated union (`clean` / `dirty` / `saving` / `saving+queued`) so `commit()`
> can only be entered from `dirty` — single-flight is structural, not flag-guarded. An edit that lands
> mid-flight is queued (only the latest survives) and drained the moment the in-flight write settles,
> never substituted for it. A refusal restores the value and returns to `dirty` **without** re-arming
> the debounce (owner decision: no auto-retry — a write that keeps failing costs exactly one attempt
> per user action; the next attempt is the user's next keystroke or an explicit Save). Relay prop types
> widened in `TodoItem.tsx`, `TemplateEditor.tsx`, `TodoCreateForm.tsx` to match the new return type.
>
> **`ProjectSettingsPane.tsx`** gained a single-flight write queue (owner decision: drains, never
> aborts an in-flight write) that coalesces a queued write with any not-yet-started write sharing a
> key — `edit` keys on the command row so repeated edits to the same command replace each other while
> still queued, every other caller keeps its own slot — and reloads exactly once when the queue drains,
> closing the out-of-order-`reload()` window S25-F1 commit 1 left open.
>

> **LATEST (2026-08-23): E2E CI PARALLELIZED INTO A FOUR-WAY SHARD MATRIX — infra change, `Done —
> pending verify` (not pushed).** `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`'s `e2e` job ran serially at ~22–23 min
> wall-clock. Real timing from a completed run (`gh run view 32596821780 --json jobs`, re-derived
> from each step's own `startedAt`/`completedAt`): the fixed setup/build cost (~660s — system deps,
> toolchain, an **unpinned, never-cacheable** `cargo install tauri-cli --locked` alone worth 321s,
> then the app/CLI/lead-agent build inside `onPrepare`) and the spec-execution cost (~617s, from
> WebdriverIO's own `17 passed, 17 total ... in 00:10:17`) are close enough in magnitude that a
> "build once, fan test-only shards out from a second job" pipeline would lose to N fully
> independent shard jobs — it would serialize the ~11 min build in front of shard time instead of
> letting GitHub Actions run everything concurrently across separate runners for free. Fixed:
> `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]` / `fail-fast: false`, each shard a complete, unmodified copy
> of the existing pipeline slicing the 17 specs via WebdriverIO's own `--shard current/total`
> (confirmed real and shipped on the exact installed `@wdio/cli@9.30.0` by reading the package
> source directly, not assumed). Two required companion fixes: pinned the previously-floating
> `tauri-cli` to `2.11.4` (matching `crates/app/Cargo.toml`'s `tauri = "2.11.2"`) behind
> `actions/cache@v6`, so the 321s is paid once per pin bump instead of on every one of the four
> shards; renamed the failure-log artifact `e2e-logs` → `e2e-logs-${{ matrix.shard }}`, since
> `actions/upload-artifact@v4+` hard-errors on two jobs uploading the same name in one run.
> **Found and fixed in local verification, not assumed away:** the first draft read `pnpm test --
> --shard …` — pnpm forwards that literal `--` rather than stripping it, so wdio's yargs parser
> treated everything after it as positional and silently dropped `--shard`, meaning every shard
> would have quietly run all 17 specs and still reported green. Fixed by dropping the `--`; verified
> with a real `xvfb-run pnpm -C e2e test --shard 1/4` run, which built the app once and reported
> `Spec Files: 4 passed, 4 total` / `Shard: 1 / 4` — the correct first-of-four slice. `pnpm -C e2e
> typecheck` stayed green (`e2e/wdio.conf.ts` itself is untouched). Full reasoning, the timing
> evidence, and the slicing-algorithm read (`@wdio/config`'s `ConfigParser.shard()`, a deterministic
> gapless partition) are recorded in `plan/e2e/e2e-00-harness-and-ci.md`.
>

> **LATEST (2026-08-22): PR #173'S OWN DECLARED GAPS CLOSED, AND A REGRESSION SHIPPED BY THAT SAME PR FOUND AND FIXED — `Done — pending verify`.** Uncommitted on `main` `f0691b8`. PR #173 (merged `3e86273`, the 2026-08-19 entry below) left three things open in its own write-up: the servers-before-reap ordering had no test because there was no seam to drive it from, the pre-existing `ThemeSettings.test.tsx` frontend flake was diagnosed but not fixed, and `deny.toml`'s `[graph] exclude` was never revisited. This session closes all three, and in re-verifying PR #173's own premises against the real code — not against its write-up — found that one of its two fixes never got the runtime check its own gate called for, and had shipped broken.
>
> **1. The regression: `process_group(0)` does not detach a controlling terminal.** PR #173's `crates/sys`/`crates/exec` fix (entry below, item 1) put every `shellenv`/`agents` child in a process group of its own via `.process_group(0)`, but a child in a *new* group still inherits whichever controlling terminal the caller's *session* has, and that new group is never the terminal's foreground group. An interactive login shell's own job-control startup calls `tcsetpgrp()` on that terminal regardless of what its stdio is wired to, and a background-group process doing that is stopped by `SIGTTOU` — indefinitely, since nothing here ever makes it the foreground group again. Reproduced directly: `script -qec "cargo test -p soloist-sys --test shellenv" /dev/null` (a real pty) **FAILED at 10.63s** — the capture ran, hit its own time limit, and was killed; the identical test with no tty always passed, which is why CI's non-interactive runners never saw it. Effect in the running app: launched from a terminal, `$SHELL`-based environment capture and agent-CLI detection both silently fall back to their no-answer path, so every agent CLI on the roster reads `Unknown`.
>
> **Fix: `setsid()` from a `pre_exec` hook, replacing `.process_group(0)`, in `crates/exec/src/lib.rs`** — the one crate `pty`/`sys`/`git`/`forge` all route contained execution through. The child is still the leader of its own process group (`killpg` teardown unchanged); `setsid()` additionally gives it a session with no controlling terminal at all, so the `tcsetpgrp()` call has nothing to reach. `nix`'s `process` feature was added to `crates/exec` for it. Two new tests, both **verified in this session to fail against the unfixed code, not merely written and left green**: `crates/exec/src/lib_tests.rs::a_run_leads_a_session_of_its_own` reads `/proc/$$/stat`'s session field from inside the run and asserts it differs from the caller's own — reverted to `.process_group(0)` in a disposable worktree (this session's own check, not taken on faith), it fails with `left: Pid(N) right: Pid(N)` (session unchanged), exactly the defect; restored, it passes. `crates/sys/tests/shellenv_controlling_terminal.rs` reproduces the regression directly rather than only the property that closes it: it gives *itself* a real pseudo-terminal as controlling terminal (`setsid()` then opening the pty slave by path — `harness = false`, since `setsid()` is a per-thread syscall the libtest worker threads don't sit on the right thread for) and runs a real capture inside that session. Re-run post-fix, this session: `script -qec "cargo test -p soloist-sys --test shellenv" /dev/null` **ok, 0.31s** (recorded elsewhere as 0.37s — both comfortably under the 1s "answered normally" bound the new test asserts; the difference is host-load noise).
>
> **2. > **LATEST (2026-08-19): TWO LOCKED-INVARIANT VIOLATIONS FROM THE DSA AUDIT — fixed, `Done — pending verify`.** Branch `fix/process-group-and-shutdown-invariants` off `main` `12d6269`, two commits (`2d34d4d`, `0c67ef3`). Both were ranked HIGH in the audit's priority section and independently confirmed by a second reader before any code was written; both premises were re-verified against the real code in this session, not taken from the audit.
>
> **1. `crates/sys` killed a bare PID (`2d34d4d`).** `grep process_group crates/sys/src/**` returned nothing: neither `shellenv::capture_env` nor `agents::probe_version` set `process_group(0)`, so each child joined **the app's own** process group and `killpg` was not available as a fix without changing the spawn. Both run `$SHELL -ilc` — an interactive login shell that sources the user's rc files precisely because version managers live there — so anything those files background survived the `child.kill()` and reparented to init. `crates/sys` was the one external-program-running adapter not depending on `soloist-exec`, which has spawned into a fresh group, group-killed and guaranteed a reap since it was written, and which `pty`/`git`/`forge` all already take. Two further holes on the same path, both `shellenv`-only: an **uncapped** `read_to_end` on stdout, and a `reader.join()` after a timeout that reaped only the shell — an rc-file background job still holding the write end of that pipe made the "timeout" block indefinitely. Containment group-kills *before* joining the capture thread, which is what makes the deadline mean anything.
>
> Also folded in (owner decision, and the audit's stated condition): `login_shell()` was **byte-identical** in `crates/pty/src/lib.rs` and `crates/sys/src/shellenv.rs` with `FALLBACK_SHELL` duplicated, and both doc comments asserted *as load-bearing* that the two resolve to the same shell — a promise two copies cannot keep. It now lives once in `crates/exec/src/shell.rs`, the only crate both depend on (`pty → sys` and `sys → pty` are both indefensible adapter edges, and `exec/src/lib.rs` was already at 384 lines, so it got its own file rather than growing that one). `crates/sys` no longer needs `nix` at runtime (moved to dev-deps); `crates/pty` no longer needs the `nix` `user` feature — evidenced by `grep -rn "Uid\|User\|getpwnam\|passwd" crates/pty/` returning nothing, not by the build passing (feature unification would have masked that).
>
> **Behaviour decision recorded:** a `--version` that outruns its output ceiling reports `Detection::Installed` — it demonstrably ran, and reporting absent would be exactly the false absence that module's doc warns against. `crates/sys` gained a stdout pipe it did not have (`exec` always pipes), bounded at 64 KiB for the probe and 2 MiB for the capture (`getconf ARG_MAX` on this host = 2097152, so no real environment reaches it).
>
> **2. The exit path never stopped the MCP/HTTP servers before reaping (`0c67ef3`).** The whole `RunEvent::ExitRequested` hook reaped process groups and called `remove_runtime()`; it never touched `IntegrationServers`, which owned each server's `CancellationToken` but exposed only `apply` — a *settings* verb, no lifecycle verb. So both accept loops stayed live across the entire reap, and `StartProcess`/`SpawnAgent`/`SpawnProcess` are reachable on that path (the core does not gate them: `begin_shutdown`'s only reader is `auto_restart_after_crash`). A start accepted in that window creates a process group the reap has already walked past — the "no orphans on quit" clause. The socket unlink lives on the cancel arm that never fired, so it never ran; the `remove_runtime` hand-copy in `lib.rs` existed *because* the HTTP server was never told to stop. `IntegrationServers` now has a closed `Lifecycle { Serving, Stopped }` and a `shutdown()` that drains every live run; `apply` is a no-op once stopped, so a toggle saved while quitting cannot raise a socket the exit path already took down. The wait is **bounded** (`SERVER_SHUTDOWN_GRACE`, 3s — owner decision) and the reap proceeds regardless. The IPC server now takes `Arc<Facade>` instead of pulling it out of Tauri's state map three times (once *per request*, inside the connection loop) while its HTTP sibling was handed the same `Arc` by the composition root; the cancellation token is threaded into the connection loop so a stop also reaches already-accepted connections, with an in-flight request allowed to finish.
>
> **Scope honoured, not widened:** the audit's sub-claim that a leftover socket makes a client "connect to a dead endpoint instead of getting 'not running'" was **rejected** by the verifier and is not implemented or tested — `crates/mcp/src/client.rs` maps any connect failure to `NotRunning`, so the stale file is cosmetic. It is fixed as ownership hygiene only. No core change, no new port, no `CorePorts` field, `build_facade` untouched; no `Facade`-level closed gate was added (that is a core decision, deliberately out of scope).
>
> **Evidence.** 9 new tests, every one proven able to fail. Observed RED on genuinely unfixed code: `a_capture_whose_output_pipe_is_held_open_still_ends_within_its_time_limit` (took 10.004s against a 1s limit — the `reader.join()` hang), `a_probe_that_reaches_no_answer_leaves_nothing_of_its_process_group_behind` (`killpg` → `Ok(())` where `ESRCH` was required, because the recorded pgid was the *test harness's own* group), `applying_settings_after_shutdown_never_rebinds`, and `cancelling_stops_serving_an_already_accepted_connection` (the defect itself). The remaining four were proven by deliberate break-and-restore. `just lint` **exit 0**. `cargo test --workspace` **1975 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** (the 3 are the pre-existing `crates/pty/tests/soak.rs` longevity tests; no `#[ignore]` was added). `scripts/check-core-deps.sh` green. `Cargo.lock` diff is exactly one line, `+ "soloist-exec"` under `soloist-sys`; no `cargo update` was run and the brotli pins are untouched.
>
> **`just test` exits 1 on a PRE-EXISTING frontend flake, not on this work.** `ThemeSettings.test.tsx > previews all advanced color roles and restores the app when editing is cancelled` times out at the 5s default under full-suite parallel load, and passes in isolation (that file's 10 tests take 6.1s together). This change touches **no** TypeScript — `git status` shows the frontend tree byte-identical to `main` — so it cannot be the cause. Not fixed here; it wants its own change (raise that test's timeout or cut its work).
>
> **Known coverage gap, stated rather than faked:** the servers-before-reap **ordering** is not pinned by a test. The two statements live inside the `tauri::Builder::run(|app, event| …)` closure, which needs a real event loop and a built `App`; there is no seam to drive it from, and a call-shape assertion would have described the implementation instead of the behaviour (§15 forbids exactly that). What *is* pinned is the half the type carries — `applying_settings_after_shutdown_never_rebinds` closes the concrete race the ordering protects against — plus a comment stating the ordering is the contract. Closing it properly means extracting the exit sequence into a named `async fn` with a `crates/app/src/lib_tests.rs` driving a stand-in server that spawns as it is cancelled.
>
> **One narrow behaviour change on the record:** deleting the `remove_runtime()` hand-copy means that in the rare case where the 3s grace expires, the HTTP runtime file can outlive the process, where before it was always removed. Single-source ownership was judged the right call — the file's owner is `httpapi::serve`, the next launch rewrites it, and the CLI already handles a dead port.

Then the audit's next slice — S14-F1 (the one unbounded buffer, fed by arbitrary child-process bytes) is the highest-value remaining item, and the frontend async-discipline group (patterns A and B, which must stay separate commits) is the largest.

> **LATEST (2026-08-18): MCP `tools/list` REJECTED BY CURRENT CLIENTS — fixed and verified.** `soloist-mcp` negotiated protocol `2026-07-28` but omitted the `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` fields that version makes **required** on a complete list result, so Claude Code 2.1.233 failed `tools/list` schema validation and dropped the server's entire tool surface (`Invalid result for tools/list: expected number, received undefined` at `ttlMs`; `expected one of "public"|"private"` at `cacheScope`). Confirmed against the spec, not inferred: `schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts` declares `CacheableResult` with both fields non-optional and `ListToolsResult`/`ListPromptsResult` extending it, and the caching page states servers **MUST** include the hints on `resultType: "complete"` results.
>
> **Root cause — an override that silently opted out of a protocol requirement.** rmcp models both fields as `Option` with `skip_serializing_if` because it serializes results for either protocol era, and populates them only inside the `list_tools`/`list_prompts` its handler macros generate. Those macros are guarded by `has_method(...)`: a server that writes the method itself gets nothing generated. `SoloistMcp` writes **both** — `list_tools` to order the featured tools ahead of rmcp's alphabetical default, `list_prompts` to gate the prompts primitive — so the fields were never set, while rmcp went on advertising `2026-07-28` as supported. `prompts/list` carried the identical defect and would have failed the same way.
>
> **Fix:** `crates/mcp/src/cache_hints.rs` — a `WithCacheHints` trait implemented for both list results through one macro, stamping `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` only for peers that negotiated at least `2026-07-28`; older peers keep a byte-identical response, since they have no schema for the fields. Both handlers apply it from `context.protocol_version()`. **Values (owner decision, 2026-08-18): `ttlMs: 0` and `cacheScope: private` for both lists.** Zero TTL because neither list can be promised to hold still — the served tools are composed once at connection time from the user's feature settings, and the prompt templates are editable in the app, where nothing raises `listChanged`; both are cheap to re-read. `private` because neither list is the same for every user (the tools are the ones this user's feature groups enable, the prompts are their project's templates), so the spec's "`public` … when they are identical for all users" does not hold here. This is deliberately stricter than rmcp's own macro default of `public`.
>
> **rmcp upgraded 3.1.2 → 3.1.3** (latest on crates.io as of this date), and the `crates/mcp` floor raised `3.0.0` → `3.1.3`. The upgrade does **not** fix this bug on its own — 3.1.3's `tool_handler.rs`/`prompt_handler.rs` are unchanged in this respect and the `has_method` guard still applies — but the floor now guarantees `rmcp-macros` ≥ 3.1.2 ("emit cache hints from handler macros"), so dropping either override in future cannot silently reintroduce the defect.
>
> **Evidence.** 5 new tests in `crates/mcp/src/cache_hints_tests.rs` assert the serialized wire shape, and both were **proven able to fail**: removing the stamping reddens the three positive tests with exactly the original symptom (`ttlMs` → `Null`), and forcing the stamp unconditionally reddens the two gating tests. `cargo test -p soloist-mcp` 147 passed / 0 failed. `just lint` exit 0 (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tsc, ESLint, core-deps and core-cycles guards). Live probe of the rebuilt binary across three offered versions: `2026-07-28` → `{resultType: complete, ttlMs: 0, cacheScope: private}` on both lists; `2025-11-25` and `2025-06-18` → neither field, unchanged. **`just test` is red on one unrelated frontend test** — `ThemeSettings.test.tsx > previews all advanced color roles…` timed out at 5000 ms in the full parallel run and **passes in isolation (10/10)**; `crates/app/ui/` is untouched by this change. It matches the load-sensitive flake class already recorded above.
>
> **Note:** `crates/mcp/src/server.rs` is now **402 lines**, just over the ~400 split smell (`just lint` reports it as non-gating, with the split roadmap in `plan/06` §7). Not split here.
>
> **Next session should start with:** the roadmap in the 2026-08-14 entry below (PR #166 CI → merge, then #167/#168/#169) — this fix does not touch it. Anyone running an **installed** Soloist needs a rebuilt bundle for its own `soloist-mcp` to carry the fix; a client pointed at `target/debug/soloist-mcp` only needs to reconnect.

> **LATEST (2026-08-14): AGENT MAILBOX + CROSS-AGENT COORDINATION — review, repair, and verification pass. O13/O15/O16 are now `Verified`; O9 stays `Not started`.** **This entry supersedes the 2026-08-13 entry below, which is now factually wrong on every open point it lists.** That entry recorded work that was "source-formatted and diff-clean but **not compiled or tested**" — it did not compile. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` failed with **17 errors across 5 crates, surfacing in three waves** (2 in `core`, then 13 once `core` compiled, then 2 more once the request shape changed); CI had reported only the first 2, because `rustc` stops at the first failing crate. Both CI jobs (`check`, `e2e`) died on that one error, and `bundle`/`smoke` are gated behind `check`, so **no job had ever run against this branch** and `specs/orchestration/agent-messaging.spec.ts` had never executed once.
>
> **Root cause of the compile failure:** `crates/core/src/coordination/todo_repo.rs` imported `Comment` but not `CommentAuthor`, which `comment_create` uses; `todo_repo/noop.rs` reaches that import via `super::`, so one missing name produced both reported errors. The rest were contract mismatches, repaired to the intended shapes rather than papered over: `agent_report_completion(task_message_id, todo_id: Option<TodoId>, summary)` carried **on the wire** (resolving it in `dispatch.rs` would have put a domain decision in an adapter, `CLAUDE.md` §16); `IpcResponse::AgentMessage`/`AgentMessages` now carry `AgentMessageDelivery`, the type the façade actually returns; and a `#[rustfmt::skip]` this branch had added to the `IpcRequest` enum was removed — it had opted the enum out of the `cargo fmt --check` gate and frozen ~50 untouched variants.
>
> **Five behavioural defects were found and fixed, each with a recorded mutation proof (break the fix, observe red, restore, observe green):** (1) `mark_completion_notice_queued` was `?`-propagated **after** the durable commit, so a store refusing the notice flag returned `Err` on a todo already `Done` with its comment appended — the post-commit path is now best-effort, and the durable completion is always reported as success. (2) Idempotency keyed on `todo_id`, so a **no-todo** completion enqueued a second notice on every retry — it now keys on `(reporter, task_message_id)` via a bounded ring (`coordination/mailbox/completion_notice.rs`, cap `MAX_COMPLETION_NOTICES` = 4096, oldest dropped), with the durable flag retained as the eviction fallback. (3) Task receipts were pruned when the **sender** left, so once a worker had acknowledged its task, a lead exiting first made the worker's later report return `UnknownMessage` with **no durable completion recorded at all** — a direct violation of O16's "a missing parent … never rolls back the durable completion", since a missing parent was the trigger. Receipts are now retired only when the **reporter** is cleaned up. (4) A fired timer whose owner refused the turn was discarded silently while the mailbox reactor observed the same signal — `coordination/scheduler.rs` now emits a `tracing::warn!`; behaviour is unchanged (an already-claimed timer is still not retried). (5) **A bounded mailbox wake backstop** (`MAX_WAKE_WAIT` = 120 s, ≈120 idle samples) closes a stall this branch introduced: the classifier now declines to classify an agent it has heard no evidence from, and mailbox wakes were gated on that classification, so an agent whose provider signal never arrived was **never woken, indefinitely**. The timer path already had a max-wait backstop; mailbox wakes did not. Scoped deliberately to the never-classified case — a `Permission`-blocked agent is excluded because a wake writes a submitted turn, which would answer its permission prompt with the wake-envelope text.
>
> **Three tests were found passing for the wrong reason, which is why none showed up as a coverage gap:** `a_handoff_is_submitted_as_exactly_one_turn` stayed **green** under a mutation that turns one submitted turn into four, because its fixture check log contained no carriage returns at all — the interior-CR collapse that D-36's whole security argument rests on was untested. `acknowledged_tasks_remain_valid_completion_correlations_until_process_cleanup` pinned only the recipient direction under a name implying both (renamed to `..._until_the_reporter_is_cleaned_up`). And `agent_message_broadcast` had **zero** façade coverage — proven when an unrestored mutation left it delivering to `Vec::new()` and the full suite stayed green. All three are now covered: a CR-bearing handoff test (`facade/git_review_tests.rs`), 8 behavioural tests for `ScopedFacade::agent_report_completion` (which previously had **none**), and 5 for `agent_message_broadcast` including the project/lineage authorization boundary and O15's check-capacity-before-enqueuing-any-recipient rule.
>
> **Gate evidence, all observed on the settled tree:** `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean; `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `SHELL=/bin/bash cargo test --workspace` **1882 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** across 52 binaries (the 3 are the pre-existing `crates/pty/tests/soak.rs` longevity tests); `scripts/check-core-deps.sh` and `scripts/check-core-cycles.sh` both pass (160 module edges, no cycles); `cargo deny check` passes; `Cargo.lock` unchanged; UI `tsc`/ESLint/Prettier clean (`crates/app/ui/` is **byte-identical to `main`** on this branch). **`just e2e` green: 17/17 spec files in 05:31, exit 0**, run against exactly the committed source.
>
> **The e2e story is the strongest evidence here, and it is a natural falsification rather than a synthetic one.** `agent-messaging.spec.ts` was **red on unmutated source**, reproducibly, on two different trees: the lead fixture set no OSC title, so a title-heuristic provider is never classified, never idle, and never receives the idle-gated wake carrying its completion notice. Closed on both sides — the fixture now emits the signal its heuristic reads, and the core gained the backstop for the degraded path. The run proving the fixture fix in isolation was built **before** the backstop landed, so the normal (classified → woken) path is proven independently; a later mutation run confirms the spec still reddens under broadcast-to-nobody **with** the backstop present, so it has not degraded into passing via the degraded path. Recorded honestly in the spec itself: every assertion reads an agent's **own terminal output**, never a Soloist surface, and `e2e/fixtures/bin/{claude,opencode}` are stubs — **no real agent CLI runs anywhere in the suite**, so green is not a live multi-provider walk.
>
> **Docs and decision records repaired.** The review found spec documents edited to match the code rather than the reverse: D-36 was rewritten to bless auto-submitted handoffs with its **security rationale deleted**; O9's v1 Verify gate was softened in place to "*When implemented:* …"; `plan/05`'s timer row was edited to bless a discarded wake result. > **Known gaps, tracked not hidden:** a human **cannot read what one agent said to another anywhere in Soloist** — the mailbox is on the Unix-socket IPC surface only, no Tauri command exposes it, no `DomainEvent` carries it, and `acknowledge` deletes the record so no transcript exists to render (this is #167's whole subject). A `Permission`-blocked agent's messages stall by design; the fix is visibility, not a wake. `coordination/mailbox/state.rs` is 505 lines, over the ~400 smell — assessed for a split and **consciously not split**: the one real seam touches six private `MailboxState` fields 33 times, so extracting it would force all six to `pub(super)` and permanently export the mailbox's capacity accounting. **A residual limit in the wake backstop, narrower than the defect it replaced:** for an agent the classifier never types, `MAX_WAKE_RETRIES` (8, ≈4 s) is terminal, and later messages inherit the exhausted attempt count because the enqueue paths use `or_insert_with` — the two paths that reset it (`observe_non_idle`, and `acknowledge`'s re-arm) cannot fire for such an agent. It needs 8 consecutive refusals of a PTY write rather than one, and the messages stay retrievable via `agent_message_list`; tracked, not fixed here. `captureBackendLogs: true` forwards no Rust log lines. `remove-terminal.spec.ts` flakes ~1 in 7 runs on an XPath click wait. **Two pre-existing load-sensitive flakes make the "0 failed" figure a per-run observation, not a stable property** — `metrics::sampler::tests::the_sampler_restarts_itself_after_a_panic` (`crates/core/src/metrics/` unchanged on this branch) and `create_terminal_runs_an_interactive_shell_in_the_project_dir` (`crates/pty` unchanged; also `SHELL`-sensitive — passes under `/bin/bash`, fails under `/usr/bin/zsh`). Each was seen once across many full runs and passed on isolated re-runs.

- **GIT SURFACE FOLLOW-UP — owner-requested polish, action guards, and watcher audit — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-10, uncommitted on `main` `7154352` / `v0.13.0`).**
  - **The branch correction is exact.** `GitBranchIcon` remains inside the badge; only the `ChevronsUpDownIcon` on its right is gone. The badge itself remains the switcher. Folder glyphs are 20 → 18 px and file glyphs 18 → 16 px.
  - **Added/removed means changed files.** The core counts each path at most once per direction across staged and unstaged status: added, copied, and untracked paths contribute to `+`; deleted paths contribute to `−`; renames, modifications, type changes, and unresolved conflicts do not pretend to create or remove a path. The titlebar renders non-zero counts immediately after the branch badge, with a complete accessible label.
  - **Nested rows stay inside the rail by construction.** Tree rows clip overflow, labels own the shrinkable width, and trailing actions are pinned to the row's inline end. `ScrollArea` now exposes a `constrainContent` layout seam, keeping the Radix measuring-wrapper override inside the shared primitive instead of embedding a private descendant selector in `GitRail`. `e2e/specs/version-control/tree-actions.spec.ts` measures the rail and action right edges after collapsing and re-expanding a deeply nested path.
  - **Action availability is core-owned.** `GitStatusFacts` is the single serialized fact shape; `GitStatus::capabilities()` derives pull, push/publish, stash, and `discardablePaths` from it. Detached, up-to-date, conflicted, merging, untracked-only, staged-only, ahead, behind, and diverged states are covered. - **GIT INTEGRATION — a long exchange with a remote says what it is doing while it does it — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-09, branch `feat/git-mcp-progress` @ `98837b0`, stacked on `feat/git-commit-intent` @ `9a5d4cf`; closes todo 46's one open item).** An agent's push, pull, fetch or pull-request merge is bounded at 120 s and was answered in a 30 s reply window, so a slow one was reported to the agent as "Soloist did not respond in time" while it carried on and succeeded. A caller that asks is now told what version control is doing as it happens; a caller that does not ask is unchanged in every byte.
  - **The spec was read first, at the 2026-07-28 revision, and it is what makes this shape legal.** A client opts in by putting a `progressToken` in a request's `_meta`; a server "**MAY** then send progress notifications" naming that token, carrying a `progress` that "**MUST** increase with each notification, even if the total is unknown", an optional `total` and an optional human-readable `message`. Both parties "**SHOULD** implement rate limiting to prevent flooding" and notifications "**MUST** stop after completion". **The timeout half is permission, not obligation** — and it lives on the *cancellation* page, not the progress one: implementations "**MAY** choose to reset the timeout clock when receiving a progress notification … as this implies that work is actually happening. However, implementations **SHOULD** always enforce a maximum timeout, regardless of progress notifications". So a host that resets keeps a slow push alive; **one that does not still times out exactly as before**, and gains only the account of where the push had got to. That is the honest ceiling on what this buys, and it is why the hop Soloist *does* own was fixed outright rather than left to the host's discretion.
  - **`rmcp` 3.0.0 supports it from inside a running handler, verified against the crate's own source rather than assumed.** `Peer<RoleServer>::notify_progress(ProgressNotificationParam)` exists (`service/server.rs`), the param's `new`/`with_message` constructors are public, and `RequestMetaObject::get_progress_token` reads the token non-destructively. A tool handler can reach both because `Peer<RoleServer>` and `RequestMetaObject` implement `FromContextPart`, which the `#[tool]` macro extracts. (`reset_timeout_on_progress` also exists in `rmcp`, but it is the *client* half — it governs requests rmcp itself issues, not ours.)
  - **The opt-in is the only switch, and it is one field on the wire.** `IpcRequest::GitPush/GitPull/GitFetch/GitMergePullRequest` gained `progress: bool`, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if …)]`, so an unasked request serializes to exactly `{"op":"git_push"}` — the bytes it always was — and an older caller's bytes still read as asking for nothing. Pinned by `a_request_that_asked_for_no_progress_is_the_bytes_it_was_before_there_was_anything_to_ask_for`.
  - **Real progress, not a heartbeat.** `--progress` is added to the invocation *only* when somebody is listening (version control stays silent otherwise, its error stream never being a terminal here), and what it writes to stderr is carried verbatim. A fake tick would have kept the connection alive while telling the agent nothing; what arrives is `Writing objects:  90% (9/10)`. The invocation is a pure function (`sync::invocation`) so both halves are pinned: `an_exchange_nobody_asked_about_is_invoked_exactly_as_it_was_before_progress_existed` and `an_exchange_somebody_asked_about_asks_version_control_to_describe_itself`.
  - **Bounded at the source, and the source is the only place it needs bounding.** `crates/exec` gained a `Watch { interval, observer }`: stderr is read incrementally into a **one-slot** latest-remark buffer (a superseded remark has no reader and no value — that is the coalescing *and* the bound), drained on the wait loop's existing 25 ms tick, and handed on no more often than `REPORT_INTERVAL` (500 ms, one const in `crates/exec` that both the git and forge adapters name). Downstream every stage is bounded too: an 8-deep drop-when-full channel app-side, another MCP-side. **The retained account did not widen** — reading continues past the diagnostics cap but only the first `limit` bytes are kept, pinned by `watching_a_run_does_not_widen_the_account_it_carries_back`.
  - **Progress reaches core as a core type, never an `rmcp` one.** `Progress` (in `core/git/exchange.rs`, beside `Stop` and `Prompting`, since all four are one decision each about the same operation) holds an optional `Observer = Arc<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>` and travels on `Exchange` and into `GitForge::merge`. `check-core-deps.sh` framework-free, `check-core-cycles.sh` **158 module edges, no cycles** — unchanged.
  - **The socket learnt to carry a remark, without changing what a reply looks like.** `IpcReply` is an **untagged** enum of `Progress(ProgressReport)` and `Done(Box<IpcResult>)`: an answer serializes byte for byte as it always did (pinned by `an_answer_travels_as_the_frame_it_always_did`), and the two are told apart by shape — `Ok`/`Err` versus `note` — so neither reads as the other. The connection loop writes remarks as their own frames while the request runs and the answer always last; the request runs on the blocking pool as before and reports through a bounded channel, so **nothing about being watched can slow the operation down**.
  - **The hop Soloist owns is fixed regardless of what the host does.** `AppClient`'s 30 s is now a *silence* budget renewed by every remark, under a `MAX_REPORTED_WAIT` ceiling of 300 s — which is the spec's own "**SHOULD** always enforce a maximum timeout, regardless of progress notifications", applied to our own wire. A request that asks nothing spends the budget exactly once, across the write and the single frame answering it, as before. A remark arriving for a request that never asked is treated as a broken connection.

- **GIT INTEGRATION — the intent behind the change, and the shape the repository asks for — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-09, branch `feat/git-commit-intent` @ `7cd37d4`, stacked on `feat/git-mcp-tools` @ `723e3a8`; todo 51, matrix row VC5).** Two things a drafted commit message could not say. Entirely inside `crates/core` — **no frontend file, no Tauri command and no MCP tool changed**, so the eager bundle is byte-identical (measured below) and the surface is exactly the button that was already there.
  - **The intent comes from a lock, not from a label, and that is the whole of the design.** At draft time the core asks one question: does a running agent of this project hold a lock on **exactly one** todo? One → its title and a bounded excerpt of its body go into the prompt as what the work set out to do. **Zero or several → nothing at all.** A `TodoStatus::InProgress` was rejected as the source because nothing clears it — a todo left in progress three weeks ago would be presented as the reason for today's diff — whereas `locked_by` is process-owned, released on every terminal transition (`supervisor/actor.rs` calls `locks.release_all` on crash, on stop, on a spawn failure and on a self-exit) and cleared at launch by `Todos::reconcile`. Every one of those was read before being relied on, not assumed.
  - **The refusal is the same one the pull-request handoff already makes**, applied unchanged rather than invented a second time: `Facade::handoff_target` declines to choose between several running agents, and this declines to choose between several held tasks. Naming one of two would attribute a change to work it may have nothing to do with, and state it to a model as fact.
  - **The join is made in C8 and nowhere else.** `crates/core/src/git/` never learns that a todo or a process exists: `commit_message_prompt` takes an `Option<&CommitIntent>` — a value type owned by C9, exactly as `pull_request_prompt` takes a skeleton — and `facade/git_draft.rs` is the one place that reads coordination and supervision to build one. `check-core-cycles.sh` **158 module edges, no cycles**, unchanged.
  - **"A running agent of this project" is now defined once.** It was written inline in `handoff_target`; it is now `Facade::running_agents`, because a second behaviour turned on it and each decides something a person sees. The mutation pass then found the refactor's own gap — see below.
  - **The template asymmetry is closed by applying G-4, not by inventing a third convention.** The AI draft used to *replace* a prefilled `commit.template`; the pull-request description has honoured its skeleton since VC8 ("keep the headings, fill only what is meant to be filled, shape last under its own label"). The commit prompt now does the same: where the repository configures a template it is asked to be filled in rather than replaced, and it goes **last**, after the change, under `Template to fill in:`. Where there is none the instruction is the subject-and-body form as before.
  - **The template is resolved in the core rather than passed down by the surface, and that is a deliberate difference from the pull-request flow.** A repository can offer several description skeletons, so *which one* is genuinely the caller's choice and the frontend passes it; `commit.template` is exactly one value that version control resolves, so routing it through the webview would only let a surface substitute arbitrary text into an agent prompt. `Git::configured_template` is the single gated read both the offered starting message and the prompt go through, so the two can never differ. Cost: one extra `git config` read per draft, spent only after the draft is known to be worth making (a change made only of files a tool wrote still refuses with **1** read).
  - **Both additions are inside the ceiling, not beside it.** The intent block is capped at a 256-byte title and a 2 KiB body excerpt cut at a line boundary, the template is dropped whole past `COMMIT_TEMPLATE_LIMIT` by the read itself, and all of it is subtracted from `ONE_SHOT_PROMPT_LIMIT` before the change is described — so the existing over-cap fallback (per-file summaries) still catches what is left. The ceiling test now sweeps patch sizes with the widest context there is: a branch, a task, ten voice examples and a 4.4 KiB shape.

- **GIT INTEGRATION — version control over MCP: a feature group that is off until you turn it on — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-09, branch `feat/git-mcp-tools`, stacked on `feat/git-loose-ends` @ `07a7225`; todo 46, matrix row VC11).** An agent can read and change the repository of the project it is *in*, and nothing else. The group is `McpFeatureGroup::Git`, **default off** (G-7), and turning it on is the whole of the grant: 19 tools over a new `ScopedFacade` surface, reached through the closed `IpcRequest` match, with scope and the trust gate spent in the core exactly as the local user's are.
  - **Scope is not guarded here, it is absent.** No method on `facade/scoped_git.rs` or `facade/scoped_git_pr.rs` takes a project, so a caller has nothing to name another project's repository *with* — the strongest form of the §16 rule, and cheaper than checking an id. Which project it acts on is the session's effective one, resolved in the core. Proven rather than claimed: `FakeGitRepository` now records the working tree each call named (the port takes a root, so that is the only place the choice is observable), and `a_session_reads_the_repository_of_the_project_it_is_in_and_no_other` runs with **two** projects open — a surface that reached for "the one open project" would be indistinguishable with one.
  - **`Prompting::Denied` finally has its production caller, and it is the only one this surface can reach.** Todo 42 built the arm with nothing calling it. Both façades now go to a remote through exactly one route each — `Facade::git_exchange` (`AT_THE_WINDOW`) and `ScopedFacade::exchange` (`UNATTENDED`) — so the decision is named twice in the whole codebase, once per authority, and the publish behind a proposal inherits it. `an_exchange_an_agent_starts_never_asks_anybody_for_a_credential` pins push, pull and fetch; `a_proposal_an_agent_makes_never_asks_anybody_for_a_credential` pins the publish; and `the_local_users_own_exchange_is_still_allowed_to_ask_them` pins that denying the prompt is the *scoped* caller's answer rather than everybody's — the over-reach todo 42 recorded catching once already.
  - **Cancellation gets an identity, and the protocol turned out to offer none — checked, not assumed.** The 2026-07-28 MCP revision was read for this: `notifications/cancelled` travels client→server (a server may send it only to tear down a `subscriptions/listen` stream, and "**MUST NOT** send it for any other purpose"), the reserved error codes `-32020…-32099` define three things and none of them is cancellation, and a tool result carries no field for saying *which* failure it was. So the answer is `IpcError::Git { reason: GitRefusal, message }` — a closed twenty-word vocabulary classified once in `crates/ipc/src/vcs_error.rs` — and the MCP reply carries it as **data**: `CallToolResult::structured_error` with the discriminator beside the sentence. An agent matches on `stopped` instead of reading prose. **The local user really can stop an agent's push**: `git_stop_exchange` sets a per-project signal armed inside the gate, so the button in the rail reaches the exchange the agent started, and what the agent is told is that it was stopped rather than that it failed.
  - **The typed refusal is one code path for every tool, not a git side-channel.** `tools/reply.rs::app_error` now renders any request-caused refusal as `structured_error`, with the wire error's own fields and a structured detail's fields lifted beside the discriminator. That deliberately changes the shape of *every* tool's error result — the alternative was a second error convention for one category, which §15 forbids. `is_request_error` gains one grouped arm: **every** version-control refusal reaches the caller, because a refusal delivered as a protocol error is one the model never sees.
  - **What is exposed is what the design named, and no more.** Status, diff, branches, stage/unstage/discard (file or hunk), commit, push/pull/fetch, branch create/switch/delete, stash/pop, the pull-request surface, its review, create and merge. Deliberately absent: the agent handoff, the AI drafts, opening a file in the desktop, aborting a merge, the file listing, and stopping an exchange — every one of them is the local user's own door, and three of them exist to put text in front of a person.
  - **There is no confirmation step, and that is stated where it is spent.** The destructive tools (`git_discard`, `git_delete_branch`, `git_merge_pull_request`) say in their own descriptions that nothing asks first and the project's trust is the only guard. Nothing is forced anywhere: an unmerged branch stays undeletable, a dirty switch stays refused, and there is no force-push.

Soloist's whole identity model is per-connection — the client binds `SOLOIST_PROCESS_ID` on connect and every scoped tool resolves its project from that session. That is D4 and the C8 identity design, far outside this slice; flagged, not touched. (2) **A no-parameter tool's input schema.** The revision *recommends* `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false}`; `rmcp` 3.0.0 emits `{"type":"object","properties":{}}` for a tool with no `Parameters`, with its own `// TODO: should be updated according to the new specifications` beside it. - **GIT INTEGRATION — the recorded loose ends: `commit.template`, opening a file, and the tree's expansion — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-09, branch `feat/git-loose-ends` @ `a250f02`, stacked on `feat/git-pr-review`; todos 40/41/43/44/47/51, matrix row VC4/VC9).** Six items the stack had recorded and left open. Four changed code, one changed only docs, one was verified already fixed and left alone, and one is a design proposal with nothing built.
  - **`commit.template` is honoured, and honouring it meant asking version control three questions rather than guessing at three answers** (todo 40's unmet acceptance criterion, open through PRs 5, 6, 7 and 8). Git consults the template only when it would open an editor, and Soloist commits the message it was handed, so the template is resolved separately and offered as the text the message box *starts at* — the commit invocation is untouched, and signing and hooks are exactly as PR 4 left them. The three rules are git's own and each is answered by asking it: the value is read with `--type=path`, so the `~/` expansion `git-config(1)` documents for a pathname-typed value is git's; a relative path is resolved against `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, **measured** on this host (a template named `message.txt` resolves from a subdirectory, because a commit runs from the top of the working tree); and the guidance lines go through `git stripspace --strip-comments`, which reads the repository's own `core.commentChar` — verified by setting it to `;` and watching `#` survive. **No prose is classified**: the one status read is the `1` git exits with when a key is not set.
  - **Stripping the guidance is the load-bearing decision, and prefilling verbatim would have been a defect.** A very common `~/.gitmessage` is *entirely* `#` lines; pasted into a three-row textarea, anybody who typed a subject above them and pressed Commit would commit the hints. `-m` does not strip them (its cleanup is `whitespace`, not `strip`). What is offered is therefore exactly what git would have committed had the template been saved unedited — which for an all-comments template is nothing, so the box stays empty and Commit stays disabled, the same outcome git reaches by refusing the commit.
  - **The template read is trust-gated, which is a finding rather than a formality.** `commit.template` can be set in a repository's own `.git/config`, and it names *any* readable file on this disk for Soloist to read and put in front of the user. That is the project deciding what Soloist reads, which is the thing trusting a project authorises — so an untrusted project is refused (`a_project_that_has_not_been_trusted_has_its_configuration_left_unread`, asserting **0 reads**) rather than answered with "no template", which would be a lie. The surface does not ask either, so an untrusted project spends no subprocess.
  - **The box follows the template rather than copying it in.** `CommitBox` holds `typed: string | null` and renders `typed ?? template ?? ""`, so a template arriving after the box rendered shows up, a changed one is never left stale, and a recorded commit clears *what was typed* — handing the box back to the template for the next message. That is the shape PR 7's react-doctor findings taught (derive, never seed state from a read), and it is why this added no effect.
  - **Todo 47 — a previewed file opens in the desktop's own application, and `opener:allow-open-path` was still not granted.** Read from `tauri-plugin-opener` 2.5.4's source, the scope check lives entirely in the plugin's `#[tauri::command] open_path`; the Rust API `Opener::open_path` consults no scope. So the grant only ever governs the *webview's* route, and the webview keeps having none. What was built is a third C9 port (`FileOpener` + `NoopFileOpener`, adapter `crates/app/src/opener.rs`), reached through one core method behind the project trust gate. **This is a strengthening of D-26, not the reversal the todo anticipated, and D-26 is amended to say so with the reason and the date.** The reason no grant would have been narrow enough: the plugin's path scope is a list of globs fixed at build time under one of the base directories its schema enumerates, and a project's root is a folder the user picks while the app is running — "only inside the project that is open" cannot be written there.
  - **The path is guarded twice, in the only two places each guard can be made.** The core refuses a path that *says* it leaves the repository (`inside_repository`, no `..`, nothing absolute); the adapter refuses one that *resolves* out of it, because a symbolic link inside a repository can point anywhere and only something holding the filesystem can follow one. Asserted against real files and real links: a link to a key outside the project opens nothing, a link that stays inside still opens, and — found by the mutation pass — a project **reached through** a link opens its own files, which is why the root is resolved too.
  - **The `no-pass-data-to-parent` finding on `RepositoryTree` is fixed by shape, not by symptom.** It was one fact kept in two places by two mechanisms: the child computed "are all folders open" and pushed it up in an effect, while the parent pushed "open/close them all" back down through an imperative ref handle. Both are gone. `useTreeExpansion` holds **the folders whose state differs from the default** — so which are open is a *derivation*, a folder that appears takes the default, and one somebody opened or closed keeps that decision — and it lives in the rail beside the control that reverses it. `RepositoryTree` is now controlled and keeps only the effect that rebuilds the library's cached walk. **React Doctor 85 → 92**, all three findings gone; the one new finding it raised was mine (`exhaustive-deps`: `changes` was a fresh `[]` every render) and is fixed by a named empty constant.

The two kinds of rollup entry share the name of **no** field — `CheckRun` says `name`/`status`/`conclusion`/`detailsUrl`, `StatusContext` says `context`/`state`/`targetUrl` — so both shapes are read, told apart by the `__typename` the service stamps. Pinned by `a_conclusion_the_service_has_newly_learnt_to_say_does_not_take_the_other_checks_with_it`.

That is why `url` is `Option`: a submitted review's summary has **no address on the service at all** (measured — `gh pr view --json reviews` carries `id`, `author`, `body`, `state`, `submittedAt` and no `url`), which is also why a thread is named by its `id` and never by its address.

But `gh api` resolves its host from **the account's default**, not from the repository: read directly from `cli/cli`'s `pkg/cmd/api/api.go`, `host` comes from `DefaultHost()` and placeholders only ever fill `{owner}`/`{repo}`. For somebody signed in to both `github.com` and an enterprise server that is the wrong machine. A Vercel or Socket check resolves to `None`, costs **no process at all**, and the handoff says so in words rather than arriving with a silence where the log should be. Measured against a real failing job on `cli/cli`: 69,234 bytes for one job, which is exactly why the excerpt is the **end** of the log, cut at a line boundary, at `CHECK_LOG_LIMIT` = 12 KiB inside a `HANDOFF_LIMIT` of 16 KiB.

Several running agents therefore never get a guess. The surface supplies the single fact the core cannot know — which process the reader is looking at — through `handoffTarget`, and a foreign project's process is refused in the core (`a_process_that_is_not_a_running_agent_of_this_project_takes_nothing`).

All four are asserted with fake timers. Its **first** question is whether it can answer anything at all — `ForgeReadiness { Missing, LoggedOut, Ready }`, infallible by design, because every way of failing to answer *is* an answer here. Anything but `Ready` and the surface spends **nothing**: no repository read, no request (`a_forge_that_cannot_be_reached_offers_nothing_and_is_asked_nothing` asserts `(asks, reads) == (0, 0)`). It is latent on this host — recorded on todo 52 from a 2026-08-07 measurement, `$SHELL -ilc 'echo __MARKER__'` capturing exactly the marker — and live for anyone whose shell greets them. The environment is now resolved in the core and handed across the `AgentOneShot` port as data; the adapter starts a shell that reads no startup file.
  - **Dropping `-i` would not have been the fix, and the man pages are why.** `bash(1)` INVOCATION: the `/etc/profile` + first-of-`~/.bash_profile`/`~/.bash_login`/`~/.profile` set is read "when bash is invoked as an interactive login shell, **or as a non-interactive shell with the `--login` option**" — the same files either way, so for a bash user `-lc` leaks exactly what `-ilc` leaks. `zsh(1)` STARTUP/SHUTDOWN FILES: `.zprofile` and `.zlogin` for any login shell, `.zshrc` only when interactive. **Measured, not inferred:** against a fixture home whose startup files all print, `-ilc` captured the banner **three times** (zprofile, zshrc, zlogin) and `-lc` **twice** — on this host, whose `$SHELL` is zsh. So the invocation is **`$SHELL -c <line>`**: no login, no interactive, and with the environment carried the shell has no job left but parsing a POSIX-quoted line. The residual is stated in the module doc rather than hidden: `~/.zshenv` (zsh) and `$BASH_ENV` (bash) are read however a shell is started, and each shell's own documentation says they must produce no output.
  - **It also closes PR 5's open item 4.** A tool that `--version` detection found through `$SHELL -ilc` but a `-lc` draft would not could previously report "not installed" at draft time. The environment now carried is the one that capture read, so detection and drafting resolve a command the same way.
  - **One resolver, and the sharing is the point.** `ShellEnv` is assembled in `CorePorts::supervisor_ports()` and travels inside `SupervisorPorts`; `Facade::new` calls that once and hands the same `Arc` to `Agents::new`. `ShellEnv` stays `pub(crate)` (todo 52's constraint) and **no external signature moved** — `crates/sys/tests/config_watch.rs` builds a `Supervisor` from outside the crate through `supervisor_ports()`, which still takes nothing. `Agents::new` became `pub(crate)`, its only caller being the assembler. `check-core-cycles.sh` **157 → 158 edges, still no cycles**: the one new edge is `agents` → `shellenv`, a top-level cross-cutting module, so no context came to depend on another.
  - **`Agents::draft` is now `async`**, resolving the captured layer and then reaching the port through `run_blocking` — the shape `Agents::detect_installed` already had. `Facade::git_draft_commit_message` became `async fn(self: &Arc<Self>)`: the half that composes the question (settings, registry, project root, the staged diff) goes to the blocking pool through the existing `Facade::blocking`, then the run is awaited. So **no runtime worker is parked** and the Tauri command lost its wrapper rather than gaining logic — it awaits the one method. No new command, so **no capability question** (`build.rs` is still a bare `tauri_build::build()`; nothing was added to `invoke_handler`).
  - **What the port carries is data.** `AgentOneShot::run(invocation, working_dir, env)` — a sibling of `working_dir`, not a shell string, and no command-line assembly moved into core. `crates/exec` is untouched: its own doc already said "what to run, **which environment to run it in**, and what a given exit status means are the calling adapter's business", and the timeout, process group, bounded pipes and reap are exactly as they were.
  - **Degradation is unchanged from a spawn's.** With `NoopShellEnvProbe` the core resolves nothing and the tool inherits the app's environment; a capture that fails is **not** an error but the `FALLBACK_PATH_DIRS` `PATH` override, and the draft still comes back. Both are asserted, not assumed.
  - **Gates.** `just lint` **exit 0** (fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, Prettier, `check-core-deps.sh` framework-free, `check-core-cycles.sh` **158 module edges, no cycles**, schema drift 2 passed). File-size advisory **17**, unchanged. `cargo test --workspace` **1545 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** (from 1539). `vitest` **145 files / 1009 passed** — byte-identical to the baseline, because **no frontend file changed**, so there is deliberately **no bundle A/B here**: reporting a number nothing could have moved would be reporting a number nobody measured.
  - **New tests: 6.** Adapter (`crates/pty/tests/oneshot.rs`, real shells): nothing the startup files print reaches the answer, and a tool only the resolved environment knows about is still found. Core (`agents/oneshot_tests.rs`): the captured environment crosses the port, a capture that failed still yields a draft with the fallback `PATH`, and with no capture wired the run carries no overrides. Façade (`facade/git_tests.rs`): a draft asked for after a launch runs **no second shell**. One existing test was strengthened — `with_no_tool_selected_nothing_is_run_at_all` now also asserts no shell was started.
  - **Test isolation is by data, not by process state.** The environment is now an argument, so the startup-file fixture points `HOME` and `ZDOTDIR` at a disposable directory **through the environment the run is made in** — nothing calls `set_var`, nothing reads or writes a real dotfile, and the tests stay safe to run in parallel. The suite's own time limit was cut 30 s → 10 s so a shell started in a way that makes it wait is reported in seconds rather than left to the real bound.
  - **Mutation-verified — 7 mutations, each observed and restored byte-clean** (verified by recorded content digest, since the slice was uncommitted). 6 reddened exactly the intended test: `-i` reintroduced (banner ×3); `-lc` instead of `-c` (banner ×2 — the mutation that proves the weaker fix insufficient); the environment never applied to the command (the fixture tool reported `Missing`); the core handing an empty environment instead of the resolved one (3 red: the port hand-off, the fallback, and the façade's end-to-end assertion); a resolver of its own for the agents context (`calls()` 2 vs 1 — the shared-cache claim); and a draft falling back to any registered tool.

The assertion could therefore never distinguish the two, so it was **removed rather than kept as a test that passes under the mutation it exists to catch**. The layering is held by `Command`'s inherit-by-default and is observable on the core side, where the empty-map test proves an adapter that cleared the environment would be running a tool with nothing at all. Recorded here as a trap worth knowing: "the child saw our `HOME`" is not evidence of inheritance.

It is not tautological (the fallback-tool mutation fails that test), and it documents the claim in the façade's own doc comment; it adds documentation rather than independent coverage, the same call PR 6 made for `NETWORK_TIME_LIMIT`.

Shell behaviour was taken from `bash(1)` and `zsh(1)` on this host and then **measured through the adapter**, never written from memory.
