- **GIT INTEGRATION — sync, branches and conflicts — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-08, branch `feat/git-sync-branches`, stacked on `feat/git-ai-commit-message`; todo 42, matrix rows VC6/VC7).** Commits can be exchanged with a remote, branches created, switched and deleted, the working tree set aside and taken back, and a merge that came back conflicted is stated and can be abandoned. Every one of them is the user's own `git` under the user's own credentials — **Soloist still stores no credential, names no credential helper, and reaches for no `gh`** (that is PR 7 and a different layer: `gh` is the GitHub API, a push needs a git *transport* credential).
  - **Two things went wrong on the way and both changed the design. They are the most important part of this entry.**
  - **(1) `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` does not suppress a credential helper, and the first honest test proved it by hanging.** Measured on this host through the real adapter: with no helper configured a credential-demanding remote fails in **18 ms**; with an *askpass* configured and the guards added this slice, **107 ms**; with the owner's real global `credential.helper = git-credential-manager`, the push **opened a GUI dialog and was killed at the 120 s network limit**, surfacing `Timeout` rather than `AuthFailed`. Terminal prompting and helper invocation are different mechanisms and the first switch never touched the second. The test that found it also **escaped its sandbox** — it invoked the owner's real helper, which popped a dialog on their desktop and wrote a `[credential "http://127.0.0.1:…"]` section into their `~/.gitconfig`. Nothing reached the keyring (`login.keyring` mtime two days older than the run; no `~/.git-credentials`, no GCM data dir), the section was removed and the removal reported. That is a harness hole every fixture test has had since PR 1, not only this one: `tests/fixture/mod.rs` neutralised the machine's config for the *fixture's* invocations and never for the **adapter's**.
  - **(2) The fix is per-caller, and it is carried by the type rather than by a flag.** `Prompting { Allowed, Denied }` (`core/git/exchange.rs`) is decided at exactly two places — a façade method — and travels to the port inside `Exchange`. `Facade::git_push/pull/fetch` pass **`Allowed`**, because the local user clicked something and is sitting in front of it, and a dialog is the *correct* answer for them. A session-scoped caller will pass `Denied`, where every way of asking a person is closed off: `GIT_ASKPASS=""` + `SSH_ASKPASS=""` (git-config(1) makes the environment win over `core.askPass` and names SSH_ASKPASS as the only fallback, so an empty value at the front leaves nothing behind it), `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never` (ssh(1): "ssh will never attempt to use one"), and `GCM_INTERACTIVE=0` — Git Credential Manager's own documented environment equivalent of `credential.interactive`, whose `0` means "never prompt – fail if interaction is required" for exactly "headless and unattended environments … where it would be preferable to fail than to hang indefinitely" (`git-ecosystem/git-credential-manager`, `docs/configuration.md`, fetched, not remembered). **A *non-interactive* helper keeps working on both paths** — a cached token, an unlocked keyring, `gh auth git-credential` — which is the point: what is denied is the question, never the answer. **My earlier version of this applied the askpass guards to every invocation, which quietly removed a working credential path for the local user; that over-reach was caught and narrowed.** Nothing detects, requires or prefers any helper: `GCM_INTERACTIVE` is a variable one vendor reads and every other ignores. **Residual, stated rather than hidden:** a *different* interactive helper is not closed by a vendor switch and is bounded only by the time limit — which is now cancellable.
  - **Cancellation, because a bound alone cannot tell a slow upload from a dialog nobody can see.** The owner rejected shortening the 120 s network limit for that exact reason. So `soloist_exec::Run` gained `stopped: Option<&dyn Fn() -> bool>`, polled every 25 ms, reaching **the same teardown the time limit reaches** — one kill-and-reap path, two triggers — and `RunError::Stopped` says which. `core/git/exchange.rs::Stop` is the core's own signal (an `Arc<AtomicBool>`, so nothing crosses from the adapter crate into `core`), armed **inside** the project's gate so a change of mind always reaches the exchange that is actually running, and `Git::stop_exchange` takes nothing that exchange holds. **The load-bearing property is that the gate is released**, since that is what makes a stuck op look like a frozen app: the test asserts a status read completes at once afterwards, not merely that the error type changed. `git_stop_exchange` is the one Tauri command that is deliberately **not** on the blocking pool — the pool is where the exchange is sitting.
  - **A merge under way is a different fact from a conflict, proven rather than assumed.** `GitStatus` gained `merging`, filled by one extra `rev-parse --verify --quiet MERGE_HEAD` per status read. Asked always rather than only where there are conflicts, because a merge whose conflicts are all resolved is still one to offer to abandon — and needed at all because **a conflicting `stash pop` leaves conflicted paths and no `MERGE_HEAD`** (verified on a real repository). So the rail counts conflicts to say what needs attention and reads `merging` to decide whether abandoning is on offer.
  - **Where the port grew, it grew by closed enum rather than by method.** `SyncOp { Fetch, Pull, Push, Publish }`, `BranchOp { Create, Switch, Delete }`, `StashOp { Save, Pop }` — five new port methods instead of eleven, each exhaustively matched. `Git::push` picks `Publish` from the remembered status when the branch tracks nothing, so **no surface has to know the difference** and the UI's "Publish" label is derived from data it already holds. `vcs::Branches { entries, stashed }` is the switcher's one read, bounded at `BRANCH_PAGE_SIZE = 200` and sorted `-committerdate`, so the bound falls on branches nobody has touched in months.
  - **What is refused stays refused, in version control's own words.** A switch that would overwrite work, a delete of a branch holding commits nothing else holds, a divergence the user has not said how to reconcile, a `stash pop` that collides — each comes back as `GitError::Refused { output }` carrying git's account, because that account names the work in the way and nothing here could. **No auto-stash, no `--force`, no `-D`, no force-push anywhere.** One core guard: a branch name that is blank or begins with `-` is refused before anything runs, because an argument is not a place to accept arbitrary text and the caller may later be an agent.
  - **The one place the adapter reads what git wrote, and why it had no alternative.** A refused credential and an unreachable remote share exit 128; the difference exists only in prose. `crates/git/src/sync.rs` matches six C-locale markers to *classify*, and an unrecognised failure stays what it was rather than becoming a wrong claim. Also generalised: a refusal's account is now taken from standard **output** when the diagnostic stream is empty — found by a red test, because `stash pop` writes its collision to stdout.
  - **Test isolation is now structural, with a tripwire.** Every fixture repository resets `credential.helper` to empty and then names a **stub of its own** inside `.git/`; the empty-first ordering is what discards the machine's helpers (verified empirically against a planted "global" helper), and the stub recording that it was asked is the proof. If the reset ever stops working the machine's helper runs *first* and those tests hang — the loudest failure available. The credential tests talk to a `TcpListener` of their own answering 401, so no network is touched.
  - **Gates.** `just lint` **exit 0** (fmt, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, Prettier, `check-core-deps.sh` framework-free, `check-core-cycles.sh` **157 module edges, no cycles**, schema drift 2 passed). File-size advisory **18 → 17**: splitting `core/testing/git.rs` (410) into the fake plus `git_fixtures.rs` took it off the list, which is the split PR 5 recorded as owed. `cargo test --workspace` **1539 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** (from 1492). `vitest` **145 files / 1009 passed** (from 142/989). New: 12 core branch, 8 core sync, 4 exec stop, 11 adapter branch, 10 adapter sync, 4 branch-listing parser, 3 auth-classification, 8 rail, 6 branch menu, 3 sync actions, 3 conflict notice.
  - **React Doctor** on the changed scope: **85/100**, identical to PR 4's and PR 5's baseline, with only the four findings PR 4 recorded as inherited (three on `RepositoryTree.tsx:122`, `async-defer-await` in `lib/diff/highlighter.ts`). No new finding. The design hook's one flag — a `0.75rem` badge size in `BranchHeader.tsx` — is PR 2's line, copied verbatim, and was left rather than restyling a control the earlier slice measured.
  - **Bundle, before and after** (A/B by stashing `crates/app/ui/src` and rebuilding; eager set = entry + every preloaded asset + the stylesheet). **654,419 → 655,286 raw, 184,449 → 184,667 gzip (+867 raw, +218 gz, +0.12 %).** It is **not zero** and it is all app code the eager shell holds: eleven `api.ts` wrappers and the `Branch`/`Branches` mirror. The feature itself is lazy — the `GitRail` chunk carries it at **91,526 → 99,516 raw**; `DiffPane` is unchanged within rollup's re-chunking noise (338,519 → 338,460). Whole `dist` 8,461,909 → 8,471,244. No new npm dependency: the switcher is the `command`/`popover` primitives already installed.
  - **Mutation-verified — 45 mutations, 48 applications, each observed and restored byte-clean** (verified by content digest rather than by `git diff`, since the whole slice is uncommitted). 42 reddened exactly the intended test. Grouped: core 10 (the trust gate removed from every change → 3 red; the branch-name guard removed, and then relaxed to allow a leading dash; the page size unbounded; a non-repository read turned into a failure; the read gate dropped; the stop never armed; stopping made a no-op; a scoped caller allowed a prompt anyway; push never publishing), exec 4 (the pre-start check removed; the signal never looked at; a stopped run not killed; being stopped reported as running out of time), adapter 15 (nothing closed off where nobody is watching; no marker classified; an unreachable remote misclassified as a credential; `--set-upstream` dropped; the delete forced; a refusal's account discarded; the stdout fallback removed; a merge never reported and always reported; the listing unbounded; the head marker inverted; the fields split on a space; nothing reported as stashed; stashing taking untracked files; the exchange made unstoppable), frontend 14 (the switcher offered untrusted; the list read unopened; a delete without asking; publish shown as push; pull offered with no upstream; no way to stop; a stopped exchange reported as a failure; a real failure silenced; every change counted as a conflict; abandoning offered with no merge; an existing name offered as new; the checked-out branch offered a delete; pop offered with nothing stashed; the notice shown for a clean tree).
  - **Five mutations did not redden, and four of them changed code or a test rather than this report.** (a) **The branch read's use of the project gate was unpinned** — every other read had a concurrency test and this one was assumed; added, and the mutation now reddens. (b) **`disarm()` was not load-bearing and was deleted.** Nothing can observe it: the next exchange arms a signal of its own and `forget` drops the entry with the project, so a change of mind arriving after an exchange finished reaches nothing either way. Deleted rather than defended by a test that would have pretended it mattered. (c) **The "stopped before it started" test proved nothing** — it asserted a side effect that a kill races anyway, so it passed either way; it now runs a program that *cannot* be started, where reporting the stop instead of "not installed" is proof nothing was reached. (d) **Removing the kill for a stopped run made two tests *hang* rather than fail** — the same shape PR 1 and PR 5 each found once. Both now bound the child's own life (10 s) and assert the run returns in under 3 s, so waiting for the child instead of killing it is reported in seconds. (e) The one recorded as structure: **`NETWORK_TIME_LIMIT` swapped for the local limit stays green**, because no test waits 30 s and asserting the constant's value would be tautological. The *existence* of the bound is pinned by `crates/exec`'s own timeout tests; the value is a named `const` with its reasoning beside it.
  - **Skills.** `testing-guidelines`; `tauri-calling-rust`, `tauri-process-model`, `tauri-capabilities`, `tauri-permissions`; `/impeccable` (`context.mjs` + `craft-floor`; its design hook ran on every component edit); `crates/app/ui:react-doctor`. **The capability question was re-verified, not inherited:** `build.rs` is still a bare `tauri_build::build()`, so with no `AppManifest::commands` restriction every command registered through `invoke_handler` is allowed for every window, and the eleven new commands need **no** entry in `capabilities/default.json` — which still ACLs no app command. `git`'s own behaviour was measured on a real repository rather than remembered: `push --set-upstream` with no remote argument **fails** (so publish names `origin HEAD`), `switch` with a dirty tree **succeeds** unless the file differs between branches, a `stash pop` collision writes to stdout, and `for-each-ref` is newline-safe because a ref name may not contain a control character.

The ahead/behind indicator settling *is* the confirmation; a refusal is stated where the action was asked for. (2) The `Prompting::Denied` arm has **no production caller yet** — the MCP git surface is PR 10 — so its only callers today are tests. Built now because the owner directed it, and recorded here so it is a decision rather than a discovery.

(2) **No real remote has ever been reached** — every exchange was measured against a bare repository on this disk and a 401 listener, so latency, progress and a large push are unmeasured. (3) **A cancelled exchange is told from a failed one by the frontend knowing it asked**, not by a typed error crossing the wire: Tauri commands return `Result<T, String>`, so `GitError::Stopped`'s identity stops at the boundary. Before it, two owner decisions are still owed from earlier slices: `commit.template`, and the diff-pane renderer that PR 3's containment probe left open. - **GIT INTEGRATION — the AI commit message — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-08, branch `feat/git-ai-commit-message`, stacked on `feat/git-staging-commit`; todo 41, matrix row VC5).** A staged change can be described by the user's own agent tool, run once and headless, and the answer lands in the message box as a draft to edit. **No API key, no HTTP client, no LLM dependency** — what runs is a CLI the user already configured, and `crates/core` gained no new external dependency at all. Opt-in twice over: nothing is offered until a tool is picked, and the project must be trusted.
  - **The invariant it lives next to, and why it is not broken.** Interactive agent launch is PTY-only and "never headless `-p`". This is the sanctioned exception, and it is a *separate path end to end*: no terminal is opened, no session is bound, no output reaches a pane, and a run either answers within 120 s or is killed and reaped. The port's module doc says so, in those terms, so nobody reads it as a relaxation of the launch rule.
  - **Per-provider one-shot invocations were built, and that is a deviation from the design worth naming.** The design says the adapter runs the tool "via its `PromptMode`". That could not work: the tool registry is **read-only** in this build (`AgentToolRepo` has only `list()`), so every registered tool is a built-in seeded with `AppendedArg` and *no* headless flag — `claude "<prompt>"` opens a TUI with no terminal and answers nothing until the limit. So `agents/headless.rs` adds a per-provider Strategy beside the existing `resume.rs`, and `PromptMode` governs `Generic` only, which is what that field's own doc always said it was for. Every arm is cited to that provider's published reference: `claude --print`, `codex exec`, `amp --execute`, `gemini --prompt`, `opencode run`, `kimi --print --prompt`. **Copilot is deliberately unsupported** — GitHub's docs mention `-p` only in passing as starting a "programmatic session", which is not the claim needed — so it resolves to `NoOneShot` and is simply not offered, the same honesty `resume.rs` shows for Amp. A tool that cannot be asked is absent from the picker (derived `DetectedTool::can_draft`), so no surface has to know which providers those are.
  - **The subprocess discipline is now shared rather than copied.** The new adapter needs exactly what `crates/git/src/runner.rs` already had — a process group of its own, a time limit, an output ceiling, a bounded stdin, a guaranteed reap — so it was extracted into a new crate **`crates/exec`** (`soloist-exec`) that both drive. It implements no port and adds no dependency the tree did not have; `crates/git`'s runner now builds the git-specific `Command` and maps `RunError` to `GitError`, preserving every previous mapping exactly. **`crates/sys`'s two poll-based probes (`shellenv.rs`, `agents.rs`) were left alone** — they are a third, weaker discipline (no process group, `child.kill()`, and in `shellenv`'s case an *uncapped* `read_to_end`) and refitting them is out of this slice's remit. Recorded here so it is a decision rather than an oversight. `login_shell()` is still duplicated between `crates/pty` and `crates/sys`; likewise pre-existing.
  - **The prompt carries more than the diff, because a diff never says why.** Owner-approved mid-slice. It is composed to `ONE_SHOT_PROMPT_LIMIT` (48 KiB) in a stated order — instructions, then the branch it is on, then ten recent commit subjects as **style examples**, then as much of the staged change as is left. The examples are the only place this repository's way of writing a message is written down; they are introduced by a block that says outright not to reuse them, and they sit *before* the line that introduces the change so nothing in them can be read as part of it. Merges, reverts (`Revert "` — git's own generated prefix) and commits authored by a program (`…[bot]`) are filtered out: none is anybody's writing. **Nothing stylistic is filtered** — a repository that writes conventional commits keeps its own voice, and one whose whole recent history is merges simply gets no examples and still asks the question.
  - **The log read was built for PR 9, not for this slice.** A proper paged `GitRepository::log(root, skip, limit)` returning `vcs::CommitEntry { id, subject, author, authored_at, merge }` (shared kernel, since the history viewer's UI will consume it too), `LOG_PAGE_SIZE = 50` capping what any caller can ask for, `crates/git/src/log_parse.rs` over `git log -z --format=%H%x00%an%x00%at%x00%P%x00%s` — verified empirically that `-z` makes the record separator a NUL too, so the answer is one flat stream read five fields at a time, which is the only safe framing when two of the five are text a person wrote. A **merge is counted, never read**: more than one parent, whatever the subject says. `Git::history` is C9's published read; **no Facade method, Tauri command or TS mirror was added** — that surface belongs with the UI that renders it (PR 9), and adding it now would be a door with nothing behind it.
  - **What the core refuses, and at what cost.** A change made only of files a tool wrote — lockfiles by name or `.lock`/`.lockfile`/`.min.js`/`.min.css`/`.map` suffix — has nothing to describe, and is refused **from the remembered status alone**: zero subprocesses, zero agent runs. Past 48 staged paths, or past the prompt budget, the patches are dropped for a per-path summary, which is itself bounded and says how many paths it left out. Drafting is **trust-gated like a change**, not ungated like a read: what runs is an agent CLI with the project as its working directory, and an agent CLI reads the project's own configuration — the same "it runs code the project carries" that the per-project gate exists for.

- **GIT INTEGRATION — CSS containment probe on the diff rows: NEGATIVE, and structurally so — `In progress` (2026-08-07, branch `feat/git-staging-commit` @ `565f350`; todo 39).** No source changed — the probe was applied, measured, and reverted byte-clean. `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-size` was the cheapest candidate for the diff pane's frame rate. It does **nothing**, and cannot be made to: split 3.3 → 3.5 fps, unified 4.7 → 5.0 fps, both within run-to-run noise, every frame still a drop by ~18×. Main-thread starvation while scrolling was likewise unchanged (p50 186 → 156 ms, 44 → 42 of 60 samples over 100 ms).
  - **Why, with direct evidence rather than inference.** The rows are `<tr class="diff-line">`, `display: table-row`. CSS Containment **excludes internal table boxes** from size containment, and from layout containment for anything but `table-cell`; `content-visibility: auto` needs both, so WebKit computes the properties and then ignores them. Forcing `contain-intrinsic-size: 500px` across 5,636 rows moved `scrollHeight` by **exactly zero** (119,760 → 119,760) where real containment would have taken it to ~2.8M px. Same null result on `td`, `tbody`, and the table wrapper. Not a selector problem: `@git-diff-view` renders the whole diff as a single `<table>`, so nothing in the row hierarchy can legally take containment.
  - **Baseline reproduced independently.** Split 3.3 fps (p50 301 ms, 46/46 frames dropped), unified 4.7 fps (p50 208 ms, 66/66) — matching the 2026-08-06 figures within variance, slightly better on a fixture rendering ~3 % fewer rows. **`document.hasFocus()` was `true` this session**, unlike the recorded one, and paired idle controls held 59–60 fps in every state; so neither session's numbers were compositor-throttled.
  - **No functional regressions from the rule** (it is inert): find-in-page matched a token ~87,000 px below the viewport; `scrollHeight` byte-identical; 705 `HunkActions` widgets rendered and staging one hunk after a full scroll round-trip staged exactly one hunk, verified on disk. **Incidental correction to a standing assumption: split view is not two synced scroll containers** — side-by-side is one `<table>` in one scroller, so there is nothing to desync.
  - **Consequence for the renderer decision.** Containment is off the table — not "insufficient" but structurally unavailable — and no different selector or intrinsic size changes that. With a lower `DIFF_LIMIT` already measured insufficient, the remaining levers are replacing the diff component or rewriting the row layer over `@git-diff-view/core`. **A replacement must avoid table layout for its rows**, or containment stays unavailable there too and virtualization becomes the only lever left.

- **GIT INTEGRATION — staging and commit — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-06, branch `feat/git-staging-commit`, stacked on `feat/git-diff-pane`; todo 40).** The first slice that changes anything. A changed path can be recorded for the next commit, taken back out, or thrown away; so can one hunk of it; and the index can be committed or the last commit replaced. Every one of those passes a **trust gate in the core**, so the Tauri surface, the MCP surface a later slice adds, and anything after them are refused by one rule rather than by a check each remembers to make.
  - **Trust at the project grain — a new concept.** `plan/02` VC3 asks that "every mutating op is refused in the core for an untrusted project", and the app had no such thing: trust was per command *variant* only. So `TrustRepo` gained `is_project_trusted`/`set_project_trusted`/`revoke_project` over a new `project_trust` table (**schema v19 → v20**, one row per project, foreign key cascading), `TrustStore` gained the three methods over it, and **C9 `Git` holds the repo itself** — the same shape the supervisor uses — so `Git::authorize` is spent inside every change rather than by whoever called one. Rationale recorded in the port doc: changing a repository runs the repository's own hooks, which is running code the project carries, which is the same thing trusting a command authorises.
  - **Hunks are named by where they fall, not by position.** `vcs::HunkRange` (old/new start and line counts, read from the `@@` line) is the shared-kernel identity; `FileDiff` now carries the ranges of the hunks it actually shipped, so a truncated diff can only be acted on where it was shown. A request built against a diff the file has moved past finds no hunk at that range and is refused (`GitError::HunkGone`) rather than applied to whatever now occupies those lines. This also survives the row virtualization queued for `DiffViewer`: nothing about an action is keyed on a rendered row.
  - **Patches are version control's own bytes, unedited.** `crates/git/src/patch.rs` lifts exactly one hunk out of the diff `git` just produced, under the header it has to follow, and `write.rs` feeds it back over standard input to `git apply --cached [--reverse]` (the lazygit approach). Nothing reconstructs a context line, which is why the CRLF and no-final-newline fixtures pass: the bytes never went through an understanding of them. A hunk that arrived carrying its own `diff --git` header keeps it and no other, so a patch never names two files.
  - **What the core decides, and what it declines to.** Only two commit refusals are made without spending a subprocess — a message that is blank space (`EmptyMessage`) and a first commit with nothing staged (`NothingStaged`; an amend needs neither, being how a message is corrected). Everything else is the user's own `git`: author, hooks, signing, configuration. A hook that refuses comes back as `GitError::Refused { output }` carrying **what the hook wrote** — the one place a diagnostic crosses the port, because it is the user's own text and never read by anything here. `GitError` lost `Copy` for it.
  - **Discard is bounded by construction, and confirm-first.** It restores the working tree *from the index* (`git restore -- <path>`), so a staged change and a commit are both out of its reach; a path version control does not track is refused (`UntrackedPath`) rather than deleted. **There is no `--hard`, no `clean`, and no force anywhere in the slice.** Every discard goes through an `AlertDialog` first, in the rail and in the diff pane alike.
  - **The runner grew three bounded capabilities**, each on its own thread so no pipe can deadlock the wait: standard input (for the patch), standard error (bounded at 8 KiB, only where `report_refusal` is set), and the existing stdout capture. The timeout, the fresh process group, and the kill-and-reap are unchanged and now cover a repository hook that hangs.
  - **UI.** `ChangesTree` rows gained a three-state stage checkbox (staged / unstaged / **partial**, for a path changed on both sides) and a hover-revealed discard; `CommitBox` is live (message, amend, disabled until there is a message and something to record); `HunkActions` renders per hunk inside `DiffViewer` through `@git-diff-view`'s `extendData`/`renderExtendLine`, attached **by line** rather than by position. Until a project is trusted, none of it renders — an action nobody may take is absent, not disabled — and `TrustNotice` says why and offers the one action that changes it. `components/ui/tree.tsx`'s row became a `div role="treeitem"` (the shape `ProcessRow` already uses) because interactive controls inside a `button` are neither valid nor operable.
  - **Gates.** `just lint` green (fmt, `clippy -D warnings`, tsc, ESLint, Prettier, dep-direction, core-cycles 156 edges/no cycles, file-size advisory unchanged at 17). `cargo test --workspace` green. `vitest` green. React Doctor on the changed scope **83 → 85** after fixing the one quadratic lookup it found in the previous slice's `RepositoryTree`; its three remaining findings (`no-pass-data-to-parent` and friends on the same `onExpansionChange` effect, `async-defer-await` in `lib/diff/highlighter.ts`) are the previous slice's and are left for the owner rather than refactored blind.
  - **Bundle, before and after** (A/B by stashing the tree and rebuilding; eager set = entry + every preloaded chunk + the stylesheet). **646,279 → 653,694 raw, 183,121 → 184,293 gzip (+7,415 raw, +1,172 gz, +0.64 %).** The git chunks stay lazy: `GitRail` 89,990 raw / 33,465 gz, `DiffPane` 338,453 raw / 96,559 gz. The eager growth is the `api.ts` wrappers, the `HunkRange` mirror, and rollup's re-chunking of the radix modules `checkbox`/`alert-dialog` share with what the shell already loads — it is **not zero**, and it is app code the shell genuinely holds.
  - **Mutation-verified**, each observed red then restored. Adapter: hunk located by position instead of range (2 red), carriage returns stripped from the hunk (1), the no-final-newline marker stripped (1), `unstage` without `--reverse` (1), the rename's other name dropped (1), a hook's words discarded (2), `--amend` dropped (1). Core: the trust gate always allowing (3), the path guard removed (1), the untracked-discard guard removed (1), the rename lookup returning none (1), the empty-message check removed (1), the nothing-staged check removed (1), the per-project gate removed (1). Frontend: `extendData` dropped (1), the trust gate bypassed (1), the discard confirmation bypassed (1), the staged requirement dropped (1).
  - **One mutation stayed green and was a real finding, not a nuisance.** Removing the per-project gate from `Git::changing` did not redden the concurrency test, because `FakeGitRepository` only counted *reads* towards its peak-concurrency window — a change passed through invisibly, so the test could not have observed a change racing a read at all. The fake now runs changes through the same window (`inside`, split out of `recorded`, which keeps the read counter to reads); with the gate removed again the test reddens as it should.
  - **Not done, and why.** `commit.template` is **not** honoured: the adapter always supplies `-m`, so the template — which git consults only when it would open an editor — never applies. Prefilling the message box from it is a read this slice does not have (`git config --get commit.template` plus the file), and it is recorded here rather than claimed. Signing and hooks *are* honoured, and are covered by fixtures. No MCP surface yet (that is the last slice), and no e2e walk for the new controls.
  - **Next session should start with:** **PR 5 (todo 41) — the AI commit message** (`AgentOneShot` port + the headless `crates/pty` adapter + the assist-tool setting), or, if the owner prefers to close the read/write loop first, **PR 6 (todo 42) — sync and branches**. Before either: the owner still owes a decision on `commit.template` (above) and on the diff-pane items PR 3 left open. The `DiffViewer` row virtualization the owner has queued lands on `feat/git-diff-pane` and will need this slice rebased onto it.

- **GIT INTEGRATION — the diff pane — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-06, branch `feat/git-diff-pane`, stacked on `feat/git-integration`/PR #141; todo 39).** Selecting a row in the rail now opens what it holds: a changed path opens its unified diff, a project file opens a read-only preview of it. Layout per **G-6** — a resizable split at the foot of the main area, the terminal never unmounted, a maximize toggle and Escape to close, the shape remembered between launches. **Still read-only: nothing here stages, commits, or writes anything.**
  - **Core.** New `git/diff.rs` (`Git::diff`, `DiffExtent`, `DIFF_LIMIT` = 256 KiB) and `git/path.rs` (the one guard that a path from a surface names something *inside* the repository — relative, no `..`, no root; every read takes it, and a path that fails it reaches no subprocess at all). `Git::file` joined `files.rs`. `vcs.rs` gained `DiffTarget`, `FileDiff`, `FileContent`. The `GitRepository` port gained `diff` and `read_file` plus `RawFileDiff`, and `Facade` gained `git_diff`/`git_file` — `GitStatusError` became **`GitReadError`**, since it is no longer only about status.
  - **Two decisions worth carrying forward.** (1) **The core resolves the comparison, and the answer says which one it is.** An untracked path has nothing earlier to be compared against, so whatever a caller asks for the context reads it as `Untracked` and reports that back; the UI hides the comparison picker for it rather than offering three choices that are one. (2) **The cap falls between hunks, never inside one.** The adapter splits the patch where its segments begin and the core rejoins as many as fit, so a truncated diff is still a patch rather than the middle of one — and the *first* hunk always goes, whatever its size, because a header with no hunk under it says a file changed while showing nothing of how.
  - **Adapter.** `diff_parse.rs` reads one invocation of `git diff --numstat --patch`: the counted form leads and is read for one thing only — a binary path prints `-` for both counts, which is data rather than the sentence the patch form prints for the same file. Args pin every part of the output a user's own configuration could change (`--no-color --no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/`). **A rename is asked about by both of its names**, because given one, `git` sees an unrelated file appear — proven both ways against a real repository. The untracked case is `--no-index` against `/dev/null`, the one invocation whose non-zero exit is an answer; `runner::answered` decides that, and refuses a status that came from a signal rather than an exit. `read_file` is bounded at 1 MiB with git's own NUL sniff for "not text".
  - **Frontend.** `lib/diff/language.ts` (path → grammar, a closed map), `lib/diff/highlighter.ts` (the one `DiffHighlighter`), `store/git/useRepositoryRead.ts` (the read all four repository hooks now share), `useGitDiff`, `useFilePreview`, `useDiffSelection`, `useSplitLayout`, `store/useStoredLayout.ts`, `components/PaneDivider.tsx`, and `components/git/{DiffPane,DiffViewer,FilePreview}.tsx` + `diff-view.css`. Three near-identical hooks became one; `RailDivider` and the rail's own persistence became the shared `PaneDivider` and `useStoredLayout` the split reuses.
  - **Maximizing covers rather than collapses.** The split fills the area by going `absolute inset-0` over the panes region instead of squeezing it to nothing, so the terminal keeps its measured size and its scrollback and the emulator never re-lays-out on a toggle. It also means `App` needs to know nothing about the split's state — the one thing it owns is which path is open.
  - **Measured (§6), not guessed — and the library was not what the design assumed.** `@git-diff-view/core` statically imports **`lowlight` + every grammar `highlight.js` publishes** as its own fallback highlighter, which the visualizer found sitting in the diff chunk: `mathematica`, `gml`, `isbl`, `1c`, `sqf`, `maxima` and the rest. Since Soloist registers its own highlighter and shows a language it has no grammar for as plain text, the fallback buys nothing. `lowlight` is aliased in `vite.config.ts` to a stub answering "no grammar here"; **the diff chunk went 1,244.10 kB → 336.92 kB raw and 395.92 → 97.65 kB gzip.**
  - **Shiki is loaded fine-grained, and the difference was measured before choosing.** Two probe builds: `@git-diff-view/shiki` (which is what the design named) produced **302 chunks / 9.6 MB** and eagerly loads 35 grammars at module evaluation via a top-level `highlighterReady` promise; `shiki/core` + `shiki/engine/javascript` with a grammar per dynamic import produced **4 chunks / 398 kB**. The package was therefore **not adopted** (it is not a dependency at all) — the app builds its own `DiffHighlighter` over `processAST` (re-exported by `@git-diff-view/react`) instead, which is what the todo's step 2 actually asks for.

It is **not zero**: the stylesheet is byte-identical and every added byte is app code the eager shell genuinely holds — the two `api.ts` wrappers and the selection state `App` owns. Lazy: the diff chunk is **336.92 kB raw / 97.65 kB gz** plus **21.44 kB / 3.20 kB** of its stylesheet; the rail chunk is unchanged at 83.53 kB / 31.62 kB. Whole `dist` **5,619,596 → 8,434,631 bytes**, of which **2,448,385** is the 59 grammar and theme chunks — one per language, fetched only when a file of that kind is opened.

Every token was measured against the rail, the azure-tinted selection *and* the hover fill in **both** themes; worst case **4.45→4.68 (light modified) / 4.19→4.85 (dark conflicted)**, all ≥4.5:1. Letters follow VS Code (M T A D R C U), including its own `C` collision between *copied* and *conflicted* — told apart by tone and by each element's accessible name, which is why the letter is never the only carrier.

- **GIT INTEGRATION — PR 1 (core read slice) — `Done — pending verify` (2026-08-06, working tree, uncommitted; todo 37, on top of the PR 0 docs entry below).** The first code slice of C9: a project's working-tree status flowing repository → core → Tauri command → typed TS mirror, live over a watcher, with the app unchanged wherever git is absent. **No UI yet** — the frontend half is types, one `api.ts` wrapper, and one projection arm (PR 2 builds the rail).

New bounded context `crates/core/src/git/` — `mod.rs` (published surface), `error.rs` (`GitError`), `repository.rs` (the `GitRepository` port + `NoopGitRepository`), `status.rs` (`GitStatus` + the `Git` service: one cache entry per project, one read in flight per project), `watch.rs` (`GitStatusWatchReactor`). New driven adapter crate **`crates/git`** (`CliGitRepository` over the system `git`): `runner.rs` (`LC_ALL=C`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `stdin`/`stderr` null, fresh process group, 30 s limit, 8 MiB output ceiling, kill-and-reap) and `status_parse.rs` (`status --porcelain=v2 -z --branch`). Plus `DomainEvent::GitStatusChanged { project }`, `CorePorts::git_repository`, `Facade::git_status` + `Facade::git_status_watch_loop`, `testing::FakeGitRepository`, the `git_status` Tauri command in a new `commands/git.rs`, and the `domain.ts`/`api.ts`/`projection.ts` mirrors.
  - **Three design decisions worth carrying forward.** (1) **`SyncState` carries the ahead/behind counts**, and `BranchInfo` does not repeat them — the design sketch listed both, which would have been two sources for one fact. Its `Unknown` variant covers *both* "tracks nothing" and "tracks something whose position is not known here": git prints `# branch.ab` only when the upstream ref is present locally, so an upstream with no counts is real, and calling it `UpToDate` would have been a fabrication. `BranchInfo::upstream` says which case it is. (2) **`NoopGitRepository` answers `NotARepo`, and the context maps that to `Ok(None)`** — the house convention is that an optional driven port degrades *silently* (`NoopMetricsProbe`, `NoopPortProbe`, `NoopFileWatcher` all do), so a core without the adapter behaves exactly like one opened on a folder that is not a repository. `GitMissing` is therefore produced only by the real adapter. (3) **`index.lock` is handled without the core ever knowing a lock file exists** — the core may not touch the filesystem, so instead of stat-ing for the lock the reactor re-arms a *failed* read once, after another quiet window. Same effect, no filesystem knowledge in the domain, and bounded at one retry per burst.
  - **Not-a-repository is detected structurally, never from a message.** `git status` exits 128 for a folder outside any repository, but so do other faults, and the difference is only in prose git translates. On failure the adapter asks `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`, whose answer is the fixed word `true` — so nothing in the read path depends on the language git happens to run in. Diagnostics go to `/dev/null`; only the exit status crosses the port.
  - **Scope boundary, recorded rather than papered over:** the reactor watches `<project root>/.git` (non-recursive) plus `.git/refs` (a tiny tree). A project that is a *subdirectory* of a repository still reports status but is not watched, because the state that changes lives above the watched root; resolving the real repository root needs a second port method and belongs with a later slice. Worktree edits are likewise not watched in this slice — the todo scoped the watcher to `.git` state files.
  - **Evidence.** `just lint` **exit 0** (`cargo fmt --check`, clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, Prettier, `check-core-deps.sh` framework-free, `check-core-cycles.sh` **146 module edges, no cycles**, the schema drift guard; file-size advisory unchanged at 17 files). `just test` **exit 0** — Rust **1347 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** across the workspace (core 862, the new `soloist-git` suites 1 + 1 + 7), UI **132 files / 901 passed**. - **GIT INTEGRATION — DESIGN REBUILT + PR 0 (docs) LANDED — `In progress` (2026-08-06, working tree, docs only; supersedes the 2026-07-24 planning entry further down).** The git feature moves from "planned, spec lost" to "approved design, parity rows on disk". **No source file was touched** — this slice is `plan/02`, `plan/05`, `plan/01`, `plan/04`, `plan/06`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `KNOWN-DIVERGENCES.md` and this ledger.
  - **G-1 — the engine decision was reversed: `git2` → the system `git` CLI (decided 2026-08-05).** The 2026-07-24 pass had picked `git2` (libgit2 bindings) for `crates/git`. It is replaced by exec'ing the user's own `git`, on the VS Code / lazygit precedent. What that buys, rather than reimplements: **hooks, commit signing and the user's `git config` are honored by construction**; **push/pull inherit the SSH agent, the credential helpers and `gh auth setup-git`**, so the app writes *zero* auth code and **stores no credential and no token** (the same posture E8 already takes for agents); coverage is complete rather than whatever the binding exposes; and a subprocess that fails or hangs cannot take the app process with it. `git2` was rejected for being in caretaker mode with fragile auth (GitButler moved off it to system git). `gix` was rejected for now — it cannot push, and it ships breaking releases roughly monthly; it stays allowed **later** as a read-path optimization behind the same port, **only with before/after profiling evidence** (`CLAUDE.md` §6). The adapter contract that makes this safe is house muscle already: machine formats only (`status --porcelain=v2 -z --branch`, NUL-separated `log --format`, `git apply --cached [--reverse]`), `LC_ALL=C`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so a missing credential **fails instead of hanging**, a fresh process group, a bounded timeout, and kill-and-reap.
  - **The design of record was rebuilt as a scratchpad, because the original spec was lost.** The 2026-07-24 entry pointed at `.scratch/git-integration/spec.md`; that file went with `.scratch/`. The spec was rebuilt and approved on 2026-08-05 as the Soloist scratchpad **`git-integration-design`** (id 8, revision 2) — §1 scope, §2 the eight dated owner decisions **G-1…G-8**, §4 the C9 architecture, §8 the eleven build slices, §9 the file-by-file module tree. **Every open decision is resolved; none is parked.** The other four decisions taken on 2026-08-05: **G-4** PR templates = repo convention (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE(.md)`, the `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` dir, root or `docs/`, case-insensitive) **winning over** a new app-level `TemplateKind::Pr`; **G-5** hunk staging, branch ops + stash, agent handoffs and a history viewer are all **in v1**; **G-6** the layout is a persistent, collapsible **right git rail** with the diff opening as a resizable split *inside* the main area — the agent terminal never gets replaced. **G-2** (`gh` for GitHub), **G-3** (AI text = the user's configured agent tools run headless via a C4 `AgentOneShot` port, no `crates/llm`, no API key), **G-7** (MCP group `Git`, default **OFF**) and **G-8** (GitHub-only v1) carry over from 2026-07-24 unchanged. `PROGRESS.md:96`'s dead spec pointer is corrected in place and the entry marked superseded.

- **DRAGGABLE PROJECT ORDER — `Done — pending verify` (2026-07-31, branch `feat/sortable-projects`).** User-requested: the sidebar listed projects newest-first (`ORDER BY id DESC`) with no way to arrange them. Reordering is now a **core behavior** (`Facade::reorder_projects` → `Projects::reorder` → a new `ProjectRepo::reorder`), durable in SQLite, announced as a new `DomainEvent::ProjectsReordered`; the drag gesture only raises intent. Owner decisions (asked before any code): **durable `position` column**, not a frontend-only order; and a **project-owned `SortableList` primitive wrapping `@dnd-kit/core`**, so call sites import nothing from dnd-kit and the library is swappable.
  - **The whole project line is the handle, by request — no grip.** `useSortable`'s `listeners` are spread on the header row; a press becomes a drag only after **4 px** of travel, so the disclosure chevron and the ••• menu inside the row keep taking their clicks. dnd-kit's `attributes` are deliberately **not** spread: they stamp `role="button"`/`tabIndex` on a row that already contains two real buttons, and they advertise a keyboard drag this build does not offer.
  - **Keyboard reordering is a menu, not a hidden chord.** dnd-kit's `KeyboardSensor` activates on Space/Enter, which the row's `CollapsibleTrigger` already owns — an unresolvable collision on a whole-row handle. Instead **Move up / Move down** joined the existing `projectActions` source, so they appear in both the ••• menu and the right-click menu from one definition, and a project at an end of the list simply is not offered the move it cannot make. Moves made this way announce through the primitive's own live region (dnd-kit's covers drags only).
  - **Dragging is disabled while the filter narrows the list** — an order arranged from part of a list is not the user's answer for the whole of it.
  - **`SCHEMA_VERSION` 18 → 19**, one `ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN position INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. **The migration seeds nothing and `upsert` was not touched**: `ORDER BY position, id DESC` already falls back to newest-first for rows sharing the default, so an upgrade rearranges nothing and a newly opened project still leads. Only `reorder` ever writes `position`.
  - **Two rounds of the mutation pass rewrote the design.** The first draft seeded `position = -id` in the migration and gave new projects `MIN(position) - 1`. Mutating each proved **neither was load-bearing** — the `id DESC` tiebreak already did that work — so both were deleted. The pass also caught a test that **passed for the wrong reason**: `a_newly_opened_project_leads_an_arranged_list` could not distinguish the fix from `position = 0` on a fresh database, because ties break on the higher id. It was replaced by `a_project_opened_after_an_upgrade_leads_the_projects_that_predate_it`, which seeds a real v18 database and is the case every existing install hits on first launch after upgrading.
  - **Evidence.** `cargo test --workspace` **1323 passed / 0 failed** (incl. the pty test that has flaked before); `pnpm test` **132 files / 894 passed**; **`just lint` exits 0**. New: 8 store tests, 1 façade test, 13 frontend tests across `lib/sortable` + the primitive, plus 3 `projectActions` and 4 `Sidebar` tests. **Every new test mutation-verified** — list ignoring `position` → 7 red; reorder dropping unnamed projects → 1 red; migration seeding a wrong order → 1 red; façade not announcing → 1 red; façade announcing without filing → 1 red; `canMoveItemBy` always true → 2 red; move inverted → 3 red; optimistic order removed → 1 red; refused order still shown → 1 red.

- **B11 REMOVE AN AGENT OR TERMINAL FROM THE SIDEBAR — `Done — pending verify` (2026-07-27, branch `feat/remove-agent-terminal`, PR).** User-reported gap: stopping an agent or terminal left its row in the sidebar for the rest of the app session, so a long day's work accumulated dead rows with no way to clear them. **No new core behavior was written.** `Supervisor::close` (`supervisor/lifecycle.rs:173` — remove the entry first, reap the group, free the terminal channel, publish `ProcessRemoved`) has existed since Phase 3 and was already reached by MCP `close_process` (F6) and the loopback IPC dispatch; the frontend projection already folded `ProcessRemoved` (`store/projection.ts:48`). Two Rust files touched, both in `crates/app`; `crates/core` unchanged.
  - **Four owner decisions (2026-07-27), recorded in `plan/05` §12, `plan/02` row **B11**, and `KNOWN-DIVERGENCES.md` **D-21**.** (1) **Agents and terminals only** — a command's `solo.yml`/overlay declaration outlives its process, so removing one would drop the row only until the next config sync or launch re-registered it; deleting a command stays the command editor's job. (2) **Offered at every status**, because `close` reaps before forgetting, so a live removal abandons no child and needs no separate Stop. (3) **Confirm a live one, not a resting one** — killing a running child has no undo and earns the modal `DESIGN.md` reserves for real decisions, while charging a dialog per stopped row would defeat the point. (4) **Availability is presentation policy**, so the kind gate lives in the frontend's `processActions` beside `canStart`/`canStop`; the core still accepts a close for any kind, leaving **MCP `close_process` behavior untouched**.
  - **Single-source, not four copies.** Remove joined the closed `ProcessActionKind` set in `lib/processActions.ts`, so it appears in the row control cluster, the row context menu, the quick-actions palette, and the command palette from one definition — the four surfaces that already read that resolver. `REMOVABLE` and `ACTION_VARIANTS` are exhaustive `Record<ProcessKind, …>`/`Record<ProcessActionKind, …>` so a new kind or action stops the build until it is answered for; adding `kind` to `ProcessActionState` made the compiler name every call site that had to answer. The confirmation rule lives once in a new `store/useProcessRemoval.ts` (pending process **derived** from the live list, so a process removed by another surface closes the dialog while one that merely exits keeps it), and the dialog itself mirrors `RemoveProjectDialog`.
  - **Three review findings fixed before calling it done.** (a) **A destructive control was landing under the cursor that clicked a safe one:** with Remove offered at every status, a `Stopping` process had it as its *only* action, so it took the one-click slot Stop had just vacated and became Start seconds later. New `canRemove(status)` in `lib/status.ts` (beside `canStart`/`canStop`) withholds it during that transient teardown; a test now pins that Remove **never** holds the one-click slot in any state. (b) **The confirmation overclaimed:** it said removal "stops the process and everything it is running", but `close` reaps only that process's own group — MCP-spawned workers are separate managed processes in fresh groups and keep running (lineage explicitly re-roots them). The copy now says what it actually stops, and when the process has live workers it says they are **left running**, counted by a new tested `liveWorkerCount` helper. (c) **The palette path was untested** — the only surface where Remove hands a live process to a dialog *while closing itself*, two Radix overlays trading focus, which jsdom cannot show.

- **DIAGRAMS — renderer defects found by live measurement and fixed — `Done — pending verify` (2026-07-26, working tree, frontend only).** The owner reported three symptoms: some themes showed no diagram at all, working ones were blurry, and switching themes/diagrams was slow. All three were reproduced and root-caused against a **real window** — an isolated dev instance (`dbus-run-session` so the single-instance plugin did not collide with the running app, `SOLOIST_APP_DATA_DIR` pointed at a copy of the DB so live data was untouched) driven over the `agent-bridge` MCP plugin, run under `GDK_BACKEND=x11` so composited pixels could actually be captured. **The backend is not implicated**: `diagramRead` measured **2–5 ms** and `diagrams`' `UNIQUE (project_id, name)` already indexes both the list and read paths; no Rust file changed.
  - **The app palette never reached Mermaid, and the failure was invisible.** `theme.ts` resolved OKLCH tokens to rgb through a probe element on the premise that "in a real webview `getComputedStyle().color` returns rgb". It does not — per CSS Color 4 a computed colour keeps its origin colour space, so `oklch(0.275 0.013 255)` came back verbatim (measured in the shipping WebKitGTK). Mermaid's colour engine then threw `Unsupported color format`, **from inside `mermaid.initialize`, which sat outside `renderDiagram`'s `try`** — so the promise rejected, `MermaidDiagram` had no `.catch`, and the component stayed on `{status:"loading"}` forever: a pulsing skeleton, no error, no `Invalid` badge. Measured matrix before the fix: **Follow app and Base threw in both light and dark; Dark/Forest/Neutral rendered (4 of 10 combinations broken)**. Reproduced in the panel on `process-status-fsm`, which carries no frontmatter override. Fixed by a new `lib/mermaid/color.ts` that paints each token into a 1×1 canvas and reads the pixel back (the browser's own engine converts; **<1 ms for 7 colours**), and by containing every failure in `renderDiagram` so it **never rejects**. After: **10 of 10 combinations render.**
  - **Diagrams were drawn at a quarter size.** Mermaid emits `width="100%"` with an inline `max-width:<natural>px`; inside `.diagram-canvas-content` (`position:absolute; width:max-content`) that percentage has no definite containing width and falls back to the CSS default replaced size of **300px**. Measured on `architecture-hexagonal`: natural **1206×1949** laid out as **300×485 (24.9%)** in a 685×856 viewport, with `fit()` measuring the fake 300px and its `Math.min(…, 1)` cap concluding it already fitted. New `lib/mermaid/svgSize.ts` stamps the `viewBox` extent onto the markup as pixels. After: content measures **1095×1819** and fits at **0.457**, filling the pane.
  - **`will-change: transform` made every zoom a bitmap upscale.** Proven with real composited pixels (XWayland + `import`), same SVG at `scale(3)` with and without it: edge-energy stddev **0.143 vs 0.247 (+73%)**, glyphs visibly ragged versus crisp. Removed — zoom here is discrete, so there was no frame budget to buy, and the CSS spec asks that `will-change` not be left on permanently.
  - **Fit-to-view may now enlarge, to a ceiling.** Owner decision 2026-07-26: `MAX_FIT_ZOOM = 2`, so a small diagram fills the pane instead of sitting marooned, without a two-node flowchart becoming a wall of pixels. The fit math moved to a pure `fitScale` in `lib/mermaid/zoom.ts` beside the existing zoom arithmetic, so the policy is unit-testable.
  - **The fit was also racing the commit.** `handleParse` fitted from the renderer's callback, which fires *before* React commits the SVG, so it measured the previous content (or nothing on first render). Previously masked by the 300px collapse, since the cap pinned the result at 1 either way. Now a `ResizeObserver` on the content element fits once the diagram has actually been laid out — the same pattern `SegmentedControl`, `useTerminal` and `useScrollSpy` already use, and already stubbed in `vitest.setup.ts`.
  - **~1.0 s per theme switch, ~0.6 s of it blank.** Timed in-page: picker click → skeleton **+409 ms** (200 ms debounce + commit) → painted **+589 ms**. Three causes, all ours: `MERMAID_RENDER_DEBOUNCE_MS` is a *keystroke* debounce that was being applied to a discrete picker change (now applied to typing only, via `lib/mermaid/useDebouncedPreview.ts`); `MermaidDiagram` unmounted the SVG on every source change (now keeps the last drawn diagram, dimmed via `.is-stale` — owner decision 2026-07-26 — so the pane **never goes blank**, skeleton on first render only); and there was no cache (new bounded LRU `lib/mermaid/renderCache.ts`, `MERMAID_RENDER_CACHE_SIZE = 12`, keyed on palette signature + source, owner decision 2026-07-26). Measured after: **cold render 560–690 ms** (Mermaid's own cost, not reducible from here), **cached render 0 ms**; a return to an already-drawn theme is **320 ms** end to end and never blank. `mermaidThemeConfig()` was measured at **~2 ms** and is not a factor.
  - **Two latent theme defects fixed while in there, both would have surfaced the moment the render worked.** (1) `darkMode` was passed as a top-level Mermaid config key, but Mermaid reads it as a **theme variable** — `Theme.calculate` assigns override keys onto the theme instance before it derives the colours it was not given, and the base `Theme` constructor never initialises `this.darkMode`, so every derivation (`cScale*`, `rowOdd`/`rowEven`, surfaces, `edgeLabelBackground`) computed light-mode even in dark. Moved into `themeVariables`. (2) `MERMAID_THEME_TOKENS` bound `noteBkg`/`noteBorder`, which **are not Mermaid theme variables at all** (verified against the base theme: the names carry a `Color` suffix), so notes fell back to Mermaid's yellow sticky — visible in the real window. Now `noteBkgColor`/`noteBorderColor`/`noteTextColor`; confirmed in the rendered CSS and by screenshot.
  - **One more correctness fix in the same function:** renders are now serialized. Mermaid holds its configuration in module-global state that `initialize` overwrites and `render` then reads asynchronously, so the fullscreen viewer drawing the live source while the panel draws the debounced one could cross-contaminate palettes during a theme switch.
  - **A two-axis code review of the branch found 13 issues; all are fixed here.** The two that were defects rather than style: (1) **the render cache could be poisoned by the very race the serialization fixed** — the cache key took the palette signature at *call* time while the render read the live palette *inside* the queue, so a theme flip in between filed a dark-drawn SVG under the light key and served it back for as long as the entry lived. The signature is now read beside the palette it names, inside `draw`. (2) **the debounce policy misread a theme rewrite that landed while a keystroke was still pending** as typing, and made it wait the full debounce — the exact delay the fix set out to remove. The rule is now the *value* an edit produced, not whether an edit happened recently. Also fixed: `.mermaid-rendered svg`'s responsive `max-width: 100%` was still shrinking the diagram inside the pan-zoom canvas (~91% on `architecture-hexagonal`), so the stamped intrinsic size did not in fact survive being mounted — overridden inside `.diagram-canvas-content`, where zooming replaces shrinking. The render state moved to a closed three-state union in the new `lib/mermaid/useDiagramRender.ts` (the previous three independently-nullable fields could spell states that mean nothing), which is also where each surface now keeps **at most one render outstanding** — the ceiling the engine's render queue previously lacked, and the only place a superseded render can be told apart from an export that must always run. Two tests that pinned call shape rather than observable outcome were rewritten to assert the behaviour they were guarding.
  - **Gates.** `pnpm test` **104 files / 601 passed**, of which **45 tests are new** (7 new files — `color` 6, `svgSize` 6, `renderCache` 7, `theme` 5, `engine` 7, `useDiagramRender` 3, `useDebouncedPreview` 3 — plus 8 added to `zoom` and `MermaidDiagram`, both measured at 8 before the change); `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, Prettier all clean. **Every new test was mutation-verified** — break the fix, watch exactly the intended test redden, restore: error containment removed → 2 engine tests red; serialization removed → the overlapping-palette test red; size stamping disabled → 4 red; cache eviction disabled → 2 red; cache separator made ambiguous → the collision test red (this one **found a real key-collision bug in the first draft** and was fixed before it shipped); `darkMode` returned to the top level → the theme test red; alpha branch and reject guard removed from `toRgb` → 2 red; fit cap returned to 1 → 3 red; keep-last-diagram reverted → 2 red; cache key returned to call time → the palette-filing test red; the debounce recency rule restored → the theme-rewrite test red; the one-outstanding-render slot removed → 2 red. The first draft of the rewritten serialization test **did not redden** when serialization was removed — it released the blocked render before the second could reconfigure Mermaid, so it never observed the race; it was fixed to flush pending work first and then verified to fail. No Rust changed, so `cargo test`/clippy were not re-run.
  - **Still open.** The owner's own real-window pass is what flips this to `Verified`. `just e2e` was **not** run (unchanged host constraint); there is no e2e walk covering diagram rendering, which is the layer that would have caught the 300px collapse, the fit race, and the `max-width` shrink the review found — all three are layout, and jsdom has none, so none of them carries a unit test. - **SECURITY SCAN FIXES — `Done — pending verify` (2026-07-23, branch `main`, working tree, uncommitted).** A multi-agent security scan (42 researchers over the ten `crates/` components × four categories, plus a breadth sweep and a committed-secrets pass, every candidate put to a three-lens verification panel) produced 6 surviving findings from 23 de-duplicated candidates, all MEDIUM. Report at `CLAUDE-SECURITY-20260722-190535/` (stamped `verified`, revision `a0c25eac9059-dirty` — taken on `feat/open-terminal` before it merged; the flagged code is unchanged at `6c51d6e`). Five are fixed here, each **mutation-verified**; the sixth is an accepted risk. The secrets pass found **no committed keys**.
  - **Infinite loop in terminal tab expansion (`terminal/parser.rs:74`) — fixed.** `execute`'s tab arm looped `while *self.cursor < stop`, but the `print` it calls resets that cursor to 0 via `flush_line()` at `MAX_LINE_CHARS`. A single un-newlined line of 65528–65535 chars followed by TAB — reachable from any supervised process's output, including via the MCP `send_input` tool — spun a `tokio` worker at 100% forever **while holding the process's `TerminalBuffers` mutex**, which every other process's terminal read/attach queues behind (UI, MCP output tools, idle sampler all freeze; only a kill recovers). The padding count is now fixed before the first space is printed, so no callee can move the loop's bound. New `terminal/parser_tests.rs` (2 tests) renders on a worker thread under a bounded grace, because an infinite loop makes a test *hang*, not fail — restoring the old loop reddens it in 10s while the tab-stop behaviour test stays green.
  - **Worker-agent spawn gate was bypassable by not binding (`facade/scoped_process.rs:118`) — fixed.** The "a worker may not spawn workers" check read `Identity::origin`, which is set only by the caller's own `bind_session_process`; a worker that simply never bound had `Origin::Unbound`, skipped the gate, and could spawn agents recursively (each a real CLI + PTY). The gate now also reads the kernel-reported peer group (`home_process()`, made `pub(in crate::facade)`). **Both reads are load-bearing and each has its own red:** dropping the peer read lets an unbound worker spawn; dropping the binding read lets a worker spawn while its OS group is not live (pgid is cleared with the group, e.g. across a restart), which the two new `scoped_tests.rs` tests pin separately.
  - **The trust review truncated what it asked the user to authorize (`TrustDialog.tsx:80`) — fixed.** Command, working directory and env came straight from an untrusted `solo.yml` into single-line `truncate` elements with no tooltip, so a padded command read as benign while its tail ran on the next start. Every reviewable line now wraps (`whitespace-pre-wrap break-all`), keeps its own whitespace so padding reads as padding, and each env pair gets its own line. Mutation-verified for the env split; **the clipping itself is CSS, so jsdom cannot prove it** — that part is unverified until a real-window pass.
  - **One-click "Trust" granted execution without showing the command (`useTrust.ts:56`) — fixed, owner decision 2026-07-23.** The sidebar/terminal-header shield and both palettes called `configTrust(project, name)` passing only the process *label* — a name the same hostile file chose — and on **first open** no review dialog exists at all (`pending_trust` only considers commands a *change* touched; `ConfigEngine::open` seeds state without publishing `ConfigChanged`). New core query `Facade::command_review(project, name)` answers what a grant would authorize on demand; a new `config_command_review` Tauri command and `configCommandReview` in `api.ts` carry it; `useTrust` gains `requestReview`, and **every affordance outside the dialog now opens the review instead of granting**. Owner chose this over also auto-publishing a review at project open. Tests: 1 core, 2 store, 2 dialog, and the rewritten `App.test.tsx` walk (shield → review shows the command → only then does Trust grant), which reddens if the affordance grants directly.
  - **F6 — checked-in `react-doctor` skill fetches and obeys a remote playbook — ACCEPTED, not fixed (owner decision 2026-07-23).** `.agents/skills/react-doctor/SKILL.md:23` (symlinked into `.claude/skills/`, with a second copy at `crates/app/ui/.claude/skills/react-doctor/SKILL.md`) tells any agent running `/doctor` to `curl` `https://www.react.doctor/prompts/react-doctor-agent.md` and "follow every step in it", declaring the fetched text "the single source of truth" for a loop that edits the working tree — unpinned, unhashed, unsigned. Whoever controls that domain could hand an agent arbitrary instructions with write access to this repo. **Accepted because** it is vendored third-party tooling that affects only developers who run `/doctor` here, never anyone using Soloist, and editing it would be silently reverted on the next skill install. Not recorded in `KNOWN-DIVERGENCES.md`, whose scope is Solo parity, not dev-tooling risk. Revisit if the skill is ever run unattended or in CI.

Now 10s, which is what "only guards a hang" was always supposed to mean. The real-shell test additionally checks its own precondition so a container with no interactive shell skips rather than fails.

- **F15 COMPLETE — prompt templates render, end to end — `Done — pending verify` (2026-07-20, branch `feat/prompt-template-render`, stacked on `fix/markdown-entity-corruption` / PR #79).** The vertical shipped 2026-07-18 stored templates and derived `{{placeholder}}` names that **nothing consumed**. It now substitutes values and delivers them by two routes. Fourteen tracked todos, each **mutation-verified** (break the fix, watch a test redden, restore byte-identical) per the CLAUDE.md §15 rule tightened during this work.
  - **Final gate, run with no agents active:** `cargo test --workspace` **31 suites / 1148 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored** (from 1049 at the PR-#78 baseline); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean; `check-core-deps.sh` framework-free; `check-core-cycles.sh` 140 edges no cycles; `pnpm test` **85 files / 459 passed**; `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check` all clean. **`just e2e` 9 spec files / 28 tests green in 1m51s** (green twice consecutively) — the templates walk closes the coverage gap it was raised for (`plan/e2e/README.md` §4 gains the row; templates were not previously a catalog entry). `specs/coordination/prompt-templates.spec.ts` (5 tests) drives the Templates preview **against the real renderer**: every declared placeholder gets a value field in first-appearance order, answering one of two keeps the literal `{{focus}}` in the prompt *and* names it in an advisory, answering the second substitutes fully, emptying a filled field brings its marker back, and a cleared description survives a reopen. Mutation-verified — dropping the unanswered-placeholder notice reddens exactly that assertion while the same test's prompt-text assertion still passes, so the two independent reports of the gap fail independently. This walk exists because jsdom's equivalent asserts against a hand-written stand-in for the core's contract; the seam it cannot reach is the one the design rides on — **the window decides absence (`delete next[placeholder]`) and the core must read an absent key as unanswered**, so an empty-string default would answer every placeholder with nothing and the core would agree. Scope groups and refused delete/duplicate were deliberately left to jsdom, which already covers them; re-asserting there costs a build per CI pass and proves nothing new. The run also **fixed a pre-existing harness flake** that had cost two whole spec files across runs (`[cmdk-root] still not displayed` — a dropped click on a lazily-loaded overlay with no retry); the agent-picker open now re-drives until the picker is observably up, the same remedy `Sidebar.openOrchestration` and `ScratchpadPanel.reload` already use, and `launch-agent.spec.ts`'s duplicated copy of that sequence now shares it. `plan/e2e/README.md` §4 gains the row (templates were **not** previously a catalog entry).
  - **What renders.** One `Templates::render` in C6 over a **single tokenizer** (`coordination/template_scan.rs`): `placeholders()` and `substitute()` consume the same `scan()` token stream, so the reported names and the substituted names cannot disagree. Escape grammar is new and tested: a single `\` before `{{` escapes and is consumed, a doubled `\\` is a literal backslash that does not escape, longer runs pair off with an odd remainder escaping. Substituted text is **never rescanned** (a value containing `{{a}}` is inert) and **never HTML-escaped** (bodies carry code). An unfilled placeholder is **left literal** in the output and named in `unfilled`; a value matching no placeholder is named in `unknown`. `MAX_RENDERED_PROMPT` = 256 KiB bounds the output, since N placeholders × large values is otherwise unbounded.
  - **Two façade doors, one behaviour:** `Facade::template_render` (local authority, explicit scope) and `ScopedFacade::prompt_template_render` (session-bound) — the MCP path never gains a `Facade` context accessor.
  - **Three delivery surfaces**, all routed to that one command: the `prompt_template_render` **MCP tool** (reaches 100% of MCP clients, including Codex CLI which has no prompts support); the **MCP `prompts` primitive** (`prompts/list` + `prompts/get`, slash commands on Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini CLI / Zed / Continue / VS Code Copilot); and a **Templates-panel preview** with a value field per placeholder and an unfilled-placeholder notice.
  - **⚠️ A security hole was found and closed in the prompts primitive.** `prompts/list`/`get` are `ServerHandler` methods, **not** router entries — and the `PromptTemplates` group's default-OFF gate works by *not registering a router*, so it does not cover them. Implemented naively they would serve the user's templates while the feature is switched off. The capability is now computed from settings inside `get_info` **and** both methods refuse independently. rmcp's `#[prompt_handler]` macro was deliberately **not** used: it auto-generates a `get_info` with the capability unconditionally enabled, which is precisely the hole. Mutation-proven — dropping the method gate reproduces the leak with the template printed in full.
  - **Four confirmed defects fixed.** (1) **Cross-project template leak** — the `Templates` cache was never evicted on `ProjectRemoved` and `projects.id` lacked `AUTOINCREMENT`, so a reused id served a removed project's rows to its successor; fixed by a supervised `TemplateEvictor` **and** migration **v17** rebuilding `projects` with `AUTOINCREMENT` (FKs disabled around the rebuild, `pragma_foreign_key_check` clean or roll back). `AUTOINCREMENT` is what closes the correctness hole — eviction is bus-driven and eventually-consistent, so it closes the growth hole only. (2) The panel **could not clear a description** — the UI mapped empty→`null`, which core reads as *keep*, inverting a contract the MCP path honoured. (3) Panel **delete/duplicate failures were silently swallowed** — no `.catch` anywhere, so a name-cap refusal showed the user nothing. (4) **No cap on template count or placeholder count** — now `MAX_TEMPLATES_PER_SCOPE` = 500 (≈32 MiB worst-case cached group against the ~150 MB idle RSS budget) and `MAX_PLACEHOLDERS_PER_BODY` = 100 (the dedup is O(n²) and runs once per row per list call; a 64 KiB body of markers declared ~8,000 names).
  - **Two more surfaced by the work.** `help(topic="prompt templates")` returned `unknown_topic` — prompt templates was the **only** toggleable group with no guide topic, and the only one defaulting OFF, so an agent had no in-band way to learn it exists; a topic now covers scope, the escape grammar, rendering and the default-OFF state. And **project-scoped templates were invisible in the UI** while being MCP's *default* scope — the panel now shows Global and This-project groups per kind, and `TemplateChanged` carries `project` so the right list refreshes.
  - **Two owner decisions were reversed by implementation, both correctly.** `plan/02`'s *"placeholder fill-in stays report-only"* was reversed to build render at all (owner, 2026-07-19). And **D-1's per-agent formatting seam was removed entirely** (todo 33): the body does not vary by client; a request parameter was the wrong mechanism regardless (caller-supplied and unverifiable — client identity belongs to the `initialize` handshake via `peer_info()`); and it could not reach the prompts path, whose request types carry no such field. Recorded in `plan/05` §12 as a **deliberate deferral with a named mechanism, not an impossibility**.

Solo's changelog says fill-in happens *"before a prompt is applied"*, but both pull paths now cover every agent — the **tools** path is model-controlled and universally supported, so an agent asked in plain language to use a template reads it, fills it from context, renders, and follows the result itself. A push mechanism would only have covered forcing text into a process the user is not driving, at the cost of a trust gate and a process picker. If ever built it is a **new capability** — own parity row, UI-initiated only, since one agent injecting text into another agent's terminal is a coordination and security hazard.

- **SCOPE DECISION — prompt-template render promoted to v1 as new row F15 — `Done — pending verify` (2026-07-19 → 2026-07-20, owner decision).** Research + audit of the shipped prompt-template vertical found it is **storage and CRUD only**: `placeholders()` (`crates/core/src/coordination/template.rs:153`) derives `{{name}}` markers that **nothing consumes** — no `render`/`substitute` function exists anywhere in `crates/`, and no API accepts placeholder values. The parity gate (`plan/02` F14:103, I13:170) scoped both rows `later` and I13's delivery note reads *"placeholder fill-in stays report-only"*, so building render would have been gold-plating under CLAUDE.md §7/§13. **The owner promoted it to v1**, reversing that note. Recorded as: new `plan/02` row **F15** (v1, Phase 8, with Verify clauses for substitution, missing-value reporting, `-32602`, and capability gating); substitution semantics as a gap decision in **`plan/05` §12** (Solo's own fill-in is cited 🟡 changelog-only at §10 and its *mechanism* is undocumented, so the grammar is ours, clean-room); and **`KNOWN-DIVERGENCES.md` D-19** for the one genuine divergence — Solo fills placeholders *"before a prompt is **applied**"*, whereas Soloist returns rendered text to its caller and **never writes it into a running process** (that needs the trust gate and was tracked separately; **D-19 settled 🟢 on 2026-07-20** — see the F15 completion entry above).
  - **Design corrections found by the plan-doc read, folded in before any code.** (a) The **MCP `prompts` primitive can route around the default-OFF gate** — `prompts/list`/`get` are `ServerHandler` methods, not router entries, so the group's gating (which works by *not registering* a sub-router, `crates/mcp/src/server.rs:246`) would not cover them; the capability must therefore be computed from settings inside `get_info` (`server.rs:279-280`). (b) A `PromptFormatter` **port with a `Noop` default was dropped** — plan/06 §5.2 step 5 forbids defining a port before it has a caller, and per plan/06 §4 the Registry/Strategy triggers have not fired (one substitution algorithm; two of four per-agent formatters are identity). The prescribed shape is the R9 precedent: a **closed `RenderTarget` enum matched exhaustively**. (c) Not one façade method but **two** over one aggregate method — `Facade::template_render` (local authority) and `ScopedFacade::prompt_template_render` (session-bound), since CLAUDE.md §16 forbids handing a scope-limited caller a `Facade` context accessor. (d) plan/06 §5.3 is **incomplete vs the built architecture**: an MCP tool reaches core over IPC, so each also needs `IpcRequest`/`IpcResponse` variants, a `dispatch.rs` arm, and a protocol round-trip test. (e) Scope stays **`kind = Prompt` only** — widening to Scratchpad/Todo would reverse resolved decision 4 (`plan/05` §12). (f) `coordination/template.rs` is **389 lines against the ~400 smell**, so render lands in a sibling module up front, per the `todo.rs` 605→335 precedent.
